Model.*\nimport caseapp.*\nimport kyo.*\n\n/** Subcommands.\n  *\n  * `run` measures one leg and stores it. `compare` and `show` read stored runs and never measure, which is what makes a reading\n  * reproducible: the same two run ids always produce the same verdict.\n  */\n@AppName(\"bench\")\ncase class RunOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"throwaway worktree to measure in; must not be the primary one\")\n    worktree: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"session id from a previous leg; omit to open a new session, which measures this machine's drift first\")\n    session: Option[String] = None,\n    @HelpMessage(\"row used to measure session drift when opening one\")\n    driftRow: String = \"suspensionBaseline\",\n    @HelpMessage(\"label for this leg, e.g. control or variant\")\n    label: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"commit whose sources the leg measures\")\n    sha: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"benchmark rows; omit to measure the whole class, which is what a suite-wide claim requires\")\n    row: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"JMH forks; 3 for a claim, 1 for diagnosis\")\n    forks: Int = 3,\n    @HelpMessage(\"evidence to collect: full (default) walks the whole ladder, timing measures only wall clock\")\n    evidence: String = \"full\",\n    @HelpMessage(\"where runs are stored\")\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class CompareOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"run id of a control leg, repeatable; give every control leg of a bracket to get its replicated verdict back\")\n    control: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"run id of a variant leg, repeatable\")\n    variant: List[String],\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class BracketOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"throwaway worktree to measure in; must not be the primary one\")\n    worktree: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"commit whose sources the control legs measure\")\n    control: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"commit whose sources the variant legs measure; equal to --control for a configuration comparison\")\n    variant: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"extra JVM args for the control legs, repeatable\")\n    controlJvm: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"extra JVM args for the variant legs, repeatable; this is how a configuration is compared rather than a design\")\n    variantJvm: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"benchmark rows; omit to measure the whole class, which is what a suite-wide claim requires\")\n    row: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"JMH forks per leg; 1 is usually right here since the bracket replicates legs instead\")\n    forks: Int = 1,\n    @HelpMessage(\"legs to run; five gives three controls against two variants, and three degrees of freedom\")\n    legs: Int = 5,\n    evidence: String = \"full\",\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class IngestOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"JMH json files to ingest, in order; label and sha are taken from --label/--sha positionally\")\n    json: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"labels, one per json\")\n    label: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"commit each json was measured at, one per json (or one for all)\")\n    sha: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"session id to file them under; they must share one to be comparable\")\n    session: String = \"ingested\",\n    @HelpMessage(\"rows the benchmark class declares; a json with fewer is a subset run\")\n    declaredRows: Int = 15,\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class PlanOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"stored runs on the rows you intend to measure; give several legs of the same configuration for a between-leg estimate, which is the quantity a bracket's threshold actually rests on\")\n    from: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"legs the planned bracket would run\")\n    legs: Int = 5,\n    @HelpMessage(\"effect size you need to detect, as a percentage\")\n    target: Double = 5.0,\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class ChainOpts(\n    @HelpMessage(\"throwaway worktree to measure in; must not be the primary one\")\n    worktree: String,\n    @HelpMessage(\"commits in order, oldest first, each isolating one change from the one before it; three or more, since two is a pair and isolates nothing\")\n    sha: List[String],\n    @HelpMessage(\"benchmark rows; omit to measure the whole class\")\n    row: List[String] = Nil,\n    @HelpMessage(\"legs per sha; two gives the chain a spread to threshold against\")\n    legs: Int = 2,\n    forks: Int = 1,\n    evidence: String = \"timing\",\n    store: String = \"bench-runs\"\n)\n\ncase class ShowOpts(id: String, store: String = \"bench-runs\")\ncase class ListOpts(store: String = \"bench-runs\")\n\nobject Cli:\n\n    val markerSpecs = Seq(\n        (\"SuspendWith\", \"SuspendWith\", \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/main/scala/kyo/kernel/proto/Arrow.scala\"),\n        (\"applyFolded\", \"applyFolded\", \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/main/scala/kyo/kernel/proto/Arrow.scala\"),\n        (\"partial\", \"def partial\", \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/main/scala/kyo/kernel/proto/Eval.scala\")\n    )\n\n    val protoPaths = Seq(\n        \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/main/scala/kyo/kernel/proto\",\n        \"kyo-kernel2/shared/src/test/scala/kyo/kernel/proto\"\n    )\n\n    def parseEvidence(s: String)(using Frame): Evidence < Abort[Bench.BracketFailed] =\n        s.toLowerCase match\n            case \"full\"   => Evidence.Full\n            case \"timing\" => Evidence.Timing\n            case other    => Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"unknown evidence '$other'; use full or timing\"))\n\n    /** How a failure reaches the operator.\n      *\n      * An expected failure is a diagnosis: one block of text saying what was wrong and what to do,\n      * then exit 1. Left to the default path it arrives instead as `Failure(Bench$BracketFailed: ...)`\n      * followed by the same text again under `Exception in thread \"main\"`, because the app runner\n      * prints the result and then rethrows any Throwable error. Two renders of one problem, both\n      * wearing an internal class name, is what a reader learns to skim.\n      *\n      * A panic is the opposite case and keeps its stack, because it is a defect in this harness rather\n      * than a mistake at the command line, and the frames are the only thing that locates it.\n      */\n    def guard[A](v: A < (Async & Scope & Abort[Any]))(using Frame): Unit < (Async & Scope) =\n        Abort.run[Any](v).map {\n            case Result.Success(_) => ()\n            case Result.Failure(e) =>\n                val message =\n                    e match\n                        case Bench.BracketFailed(reason) => reason\n                        case t: Throwable                => Maybe(t.getMessage).getOrElse(t.toString)\n                        case other                       => other.toString\n                Console.printLine(s\"⛔ $message\").andThen(exit(1))\n            case Result.Panic(t) =>\n                Console.printLine(\"⛔ the harness itself failed, which is a bug in it and not in the command:\")\n                    .andThen(Sync.defer(t.printStackTrace()))\n                    .andThen(exit(2))\n        }\n\n    private def exit(code: Int)(using Frame): Nothing < Sync =\n        // Unsafe: an application entrypoint is the one place a process exit is the correct\n        // expression of a failure, and it is what keeps the diagnosis above from being followed by\n        // the runner's own second rendering of the same error.\n        Sync.defer(java.lang.System.exit(code)).andThen(Sync.defer(throw new IllegalStateException(\"unreachable\")))\n\nend Cli\n\nobject BenchRun extends KyoCaseApp[RunOpts]:\n    run { (opts: RunOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            evidence <- Cli.parseEvidence(opts.evidence)\n            // a session carries the machine's measured drift; reusing one keeps legs comparable,\n            // opening one costs two extra runs and is what makes the band a measurement\n            session <- opts.session match\n                case Some(id) => Store.session(Path(opts.store), id)\n                case None     => Bench.openSession(Path(opts.worktree), opts.driftRow)\n            leg <- Bench.runLeg(\n                session = session,\n                worktree = Path(opts.worktree),\n                label = opts.label,\n                sha = opts.sha,\n                paths = Cli.protoPaths,\n                markerSpecs = Cli.markerSpecs,\n                rows = opts.row,\n                forks = opts.forks,\n                evidence = evidence\n            )\n            file <- Store.save(Path(opts.store), leg)\n            _    <- Console.printLine(s\"stored ${leg.id} (${leg.rows.size} rows, ${leg.evidence}) at $file\")\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchRun\n\n/** Runs a whole bracket and reports it, which is the only shape that can support a threshold.\n  *\n  * A single pair can be classified against a drift band but cannot say how small an effect it would\n  * have caught, so every flat row it produces is unbounded. This replicates instead, and reports the\n  * A/A null first: if the control legs disagree with each other, nothing below that is readable.\n  */\nobject BenchBracket extends KyoCaseApp[BracketOpts]:\n    run { (opts: BracketOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            evidence <- Cli.parseEvidence(opts.evidence)\n            session  <- Bench.openSession(Path(opts.worktree), opts.row.headOption.getOrElse(\"suspensionBaseline\"))\n            legs <- Bench.bracket(\n                session = session,\n                worktree = Path(opts.worktree),\n                control = Bench.Arm(opts.control, opts.controlJvm),\n                variant = Bench.Arm(opts.variant, opts.variantJvm),\n                paths = Cli.protoPaths,\n                markerSpecs = Cli.markerSpecs,\n                rows = opts.row,\n                forks = opts.forks,\n                evidence = evidence,\n                legs = opts.legs\n            )\n            (controls, variants) = legs\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(controls ++ variants)(r => Store.save(Path(opts.store), r).unit)\n            aa  = Bench.nullComparison(controls)\n            cmp = Bench.compareReplicated(controls, variants)\n            // the null's verdict and the steady-state verdict are the same kind of statement, that\n            // the numbers below cannot be read, so they are one banner and one exit code. Reporting\n            // a dirty null as a line of text and exiting 0 is the failure this tool exists to refuse.\n            blockers = Report.nullBlockers(aa, controls.size) ++ Report.blockers(cmp)\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                if blockers.isEmpty then Report.nullNote(aa)\n                else\n                    \"\\n\" + \"=\" * 78 + s\"\\n\\u26d4 NOT A VALID SESSION: ${blockers.size} reason(s).\\n\" +\n                        blockers.map(b => s\"  - $b\").mkString(\"\\n\") + \"\\n\" + \"=\" * 78 + \"\\n\"\n            )\n            _ <- Console.printLine(Report.render(cmp))\n            _ <- Abort.when(blockers.nonEmpty)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${blockers.size} reason(s) make this session unreadable; see the banner above\")\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchBracket\n\n/** Brings measurements taken outside the harness under it.\n  *\n  * Without this the tool can only speak about runs it produced itself, which is what drove an entire\n  * campaign's worth of verdicts into hand-written python.\n  */\nobject BenchIngest extends KyoCaseApp[IngestOpts]:\n    run { (opts: IngestOpts) =>\n        val session = Session(opts.session, \"ingested\", \"unknown\", 0.0)\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            _ <- Abort.when(opts.json.size != opts.label.size)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${opts.json.size} json files but ${opts.label.size} labels; they must correspond\")\n            )\n            // a third sha for two files means one of the three is going somewhere the operator did\n            // not intend, and the leftover would otherwise be dropped without a word\n            _ <- Abort.when(opts.sha.size != 1 && opts.sha.size != opts.json.size)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(\n                    s\"${opts.json.size} json files but ${opts.sha.size} shas; give one per file, or one for all of them\"\n                )\n            )\n            runs <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(opts.json.zip(opts.label).zipWithIndex)) { case ((j, l), i) =>\n                Ingest.file(\n                    Path(j), l,\n                    opts.sha.lift(i).orElse(opts.sha.headOption).getOrElse(\"unknown\"),\n                    session, Path(opts.store), opts.declaredRows\n                )\n            }\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(runs) { r =>\n                Console.printLine(f\"ingested ${r.id}%-52s ${r.rows.size}%2d rows  ${if r.wholeClass then \"whole class\" else \"SUBSET\"}\")\n            }\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                \"\\nThese are timing-only runs: no markers, no tree hash, no evidence ladder. The report will \" +\n                    \"refuse to attribute any movement in them to a mechanism, which is correct, because nothing \" +\n                    \"about how they were produced was under the harness's control.\"\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchIngest\n\n/** Says what a planned session could detect, before it is spent.\n  *\n  * Three runs were spent reporting a 25% timing regression on a row that resolves to ±22.6% and\n  * cannot support a verdict of that size. Each was believed at the time. This answers that question\n  * from data already stored.\n  */\nobject BenchPlan extends KyoCaseApp[PlanOpts]:\n    run { (opts: PlanOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            priors <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(opts.from))(id => Store.load(Path(opts.store), id))\n            prior = priors.head\n            fs    = Plan.forecast(priors, opts.legs, Bench.FamilyAlpha)\n            blind = Plan.blind(fs, opts.target / 100.0)\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                f\"Planning ${opts.legs} legs against a target of ±${opts.target}%.1f%%, from ${prior.rows.size} rows across ${priors.size} prior leg(s).\\n\" +\n                    (if priors.size < 2 then \"One leg only, so the estimate uses within-leg error, which is a different quantity from the between-leg spread a threshold rests on. Give more legs for a real forecast.\\n\" else \"\")\n            )\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(fs)(f => Console.printLine(\"  \" + f.show))\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                if blind.isEmpty then f\"\\nEvery row can resolve ±${opts.target}%.1f%% at this configuration.\"\n                else\n                    f\"\\n\\u26a0\\ufe0f  ${blind.size} row(s) cannot resolve ±${opts.target}%.1f%% and will report flat whatever happens:\\n\" +\n                        blind.map(f => s\"  - ${f.row}\").mkString(\"\\n\") +\n                        \"\\n\\nMore forks will not help: calibration showed tripling them moved the resolution by 0.05 points, \" +\n                        \"because the variance is between legs rather than within them. More legs, or a quieter machine.\"\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchPlan\n\n/** Isolates a source-level mechanism, which a pair of shas structurally cannot.\n  *\n  * A bracket measures the difference between two trees. Attributing that difference to one change\n  * inside it requires the partition to have been declared, and a pair does not declare one. A chain\n  * does: each step is one change, and each adjacent comparison is that change's isolated contribution.\n  */\nobject BenchChain extends KyoCaseApp[ChainOpts]:\n    run { (opts: ChainOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            // before the worktree is touched at all: a chain that is not one should cost nothing\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(Chunk.from(Bench.requireChain(opts.sha).toList))(w =>\n                Abort.fail[Bench.BracketFailed](Bench.BracketFailed(w))\n            )\n            evidence <- Cli.parseEvidence(opts.evidence)\n            session  <- Bench.openSession(Path(opts.worktree), opts.row.headOption.getOrElse(\"suspensionBaseline\"))\n            steps <- Bench.chain(\n                session = session,\n                worktree = Path(opts.worktree),\n                shas = opts.sha,\n                paths = Cli.protoPaths,\n                markerSpecs = Cli.markerSpecs,\n                rows = opts.row,\n                forks = opts.forks,\n                evidence = evidence,\n                legsPerSha = opts.legs\n            )\n            _ <- Kyo.foreachDiscard(steps.flatMap(_._2))(r => Store.save(Path(opts.store), r).unit)\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                s\"Chain of ${steps.size} shas, ${opts.legs} legs each. Each comparison below is one step's \" +\n                    \"isolated contribution, which is the only shape that can carry a source-level mechanism.\\n\"\n            )\n            blockers <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(steps.sliding(2).toSeq).filter(_.size == 2)) { pair =>\n                val (fromSha, fromLegs) = pair(0)\n                val (toSha, toLegs)     = pair(1)\n                val cmp                 = Bench.compareReplicated(fromLegs, toLegs)\n                Console.printLine(s\"\\n${\"-\" * 78}\\n${fromSha.take(10)} -> ${toSha.take(10)}\\n\")\n                    .andThen(Console.printLine(Report.render(cmp, chainLength = steps.size)))\n                    .andThen(Report.blockers(cmp))\n            }.map(_.flatten)\n            _ <- Abort.when(blockers.nonEmpty)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${blockers.size} step(s) of the chain are not readable:\\n${blockers.map(b => s\"  - $b\").mkString(\"\\n\")}\")\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchChain\n\nobject BenchCompare extends KyoCaseApp[CompareOpts]:\n    run { (opts: CompareOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        for\n            controls <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(opts.control))(id => Store.load(Path(opts.store), id))\n            variants <- Kyo.foreach(Chunk.from(opts.variant))(id => Store.load(Path(opts.store), id))\n            _ <- Abort.when(controls.isEmpty || variants.isEmpty)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(\"give at least one --control and one --variant\")\n            )\n            // A bracket's replicated verdict used to be visible only while the bracket ran. Once its\n            // legs were stored, the only thing recoverable from them was the single-pair statistic,\n            // which is the weaker one: on the replicated sweep the pair says five wins and the\n            // replicate statistic says three. So the harness's own principle, that a comparison is a\n            // pure function over records and two run ids always produce the same verdict, held for\n            // the weaker claim and not for the stronger one.\n            replicated = controls.size > 1 || variants.size > 1\n            cmp        = if replicated then Bench.compareReplicated(controls, variants) else Bench.compare(controls.head, variants.head)\n            _ <- Console.printLine(\n                if replicated then\n                    s\"Replicated over ${controls.size} control and ${variants.size} variant leg(s): the threshold below is \" +\n                        \"estimated from the spread between them.\\n\"\n                else\n                    \"One control leg against one variant, so the bound below is the legs' own error and not a \" +\n                        \"threshold estimated from replicates. Pass every leg of a bracket to get its real verdict.\\n\"\n            )\n            _ <- Console.printLine(Report.render(cmp))\n            // a non-steady-state leg fails the run rather than warning inside it. A warning is\n            // something a reader skips; an exit code is not, and this tool exists for a reader who\n            // demonstrably skips them.\n            _ <- Abort.when(Report.blockers(cmp).nonEmpty)(\n                Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${Report.blockers(cmp).size} leg(s) did not reach steady state; the verdicts above are not readable\")\n            )\n        yield ()\n        )\n    }\nend BenchCompare\n\nobject BenchShow extends KyoCaseApp[ShowOpts]:\n    run { (opts: ShowOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        Store.load(Path(opts.store), opts.id).map { r =>\n            Console.printLine(\n                s\"\"\"|${r.id}\n                    |  sha ${r.sha} label ${r.label} forks ${r.forks} evidence ${r.evidence}\n                    |  scope ${if r.wholeClass then s\"whole class (${r.declaredRows} rows)\" else s\"${r.rows.size} selected rows\"}\n                    |  markers ${r.markers.map(m => s\"${m.name}=${m.count}\").mkString(\" \")}\n                    |  rows ${r.rows.size}, jit entries ${r.jit.size}, alloc sites ${r.alloc.size}, cpu sites ${r.cpu.size}\"\"\".stripMargin\n            )\n        }\n        )\n    }\nend BenchShow\n\nobject BenchList extends KyoCaseApp[ListOpts]:\n    run { (opts: ListOpts) =>\n        Cli.guard(\n        Store.list(Path(opts.store)).map { runs =>\n            if runs.isEmpty then Console.printLine(\"no runs stored\")\n            else\n                Kyo.foreachDiscard(runs.sortBy(_.recordedAt)) { r =>\n                    Console.printLine(f\"${r.id}%-44s ${r.label}%-10s ${r.evidence}%-7s ${r.rows.size}%3d rows  ${r.recordedAt}\")\n                }\n        }\n        )\n    }\nend BenchList\n","numLines":417,"startLine":1,"totalLines":417}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"16111098-b7c7-45c6-bb36-b6f84dabadbb","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}

{"parentUuid":"f363ab96-0619-49cf-9551-3ad235db98bf","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"2193a75c-66b5-4f88-ac25-e445cef8365c","agentId":"aba808edfe8200f22","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016WQPkg3eH3gcGcRUfJwMtt","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport kyo.*\n2\t\n3\t/** What a run captured, and what a comparison of two runs concluded.\n4\t  *\n5\t  * Records are persisted as json and every comparison is a pure function over them, so re-reading what the JIT decided about a method, or\n6\t  * re-deriving a verdict, never re-runs a benchmark and never varies between readings.\n7\t  */\n8\tobject Model:\n9\t\n10\t    /** How much of the evidence ladder a run collected. A comparison built from anything below `Full` cannot attribute a movement to a\n11\t      * mechanism, and says so rather than leaving the reader to assume one was checked.\n12\t      */\n13\t    enum Evidence derives Schema, CanEqual:\n14\t        case Timing, Full\n15\t\n16\t    /** One benchmark row: the score with its error, plus the allocation JMH's gc profiler attributes to it. */\n17\t    case class Row(\n18\t        name: String,\n19\t        mode: String,\n20\t        count: Int,\n21\t        score: Double,\n22\t        error: Double,\n23\t        unit: String,\n24\t        /** The per-iteration series JMH recorded, kept rather than reduced to a count.\n25\t          *\n26\t          * A summary score hides the shape that produced it. A real control leg read\n27\t          * `[86.4, 80.8, 81.4, 78.5, 78.6]`: a warmup ramp whose first iteration inflated both the\n28\t          * mean and the error, and which the harness could not see at all because it kept only the\n29\t          * count. That leg then carried a -9.8% \"win\" that was substantially its own unsettled start.\n30\t          */\n31\t        iterations: Chunk[Double],\n32\t        allocPerOp: Maybe[Double],\n33\t        /** Milliseconds the JIT spent compiling *during the measured window*. Non-trivial values mean the JVM had not reached steady state\n34\t          * and the score describes a mixture of compiled and compiling code.\n35\t          */\n36\t        compilerMsProfiled: Maybe[Double],\n37\t        compilerMsTotal: Maybe[Double]\n38\t    ) derives Schema:\n39\t        /** Compilation during measurement as a fraction of the measured wall time. */\n40\t        def compilingShare(measuredMs: Double): Maybe[Double] = compilerMsProfiled.map(_ / measuredMs * 100)\n41\t\n42\t        /** This row's own relative uncertainty, as a fraction of its score. */\n43\t        def relativeError: Double = if score <= 0.0 then 0.0 else error / score\n44\t\n45\t        /** How far the first measured iteration sits from the median of the rest, as a fraction.\n46\t          *\n47\t          * A leg still warming up shows it here and nowhere else: the score and the error absorb the\n48\t          * ramp without revealing it. This is the only steady-state signal available to a run ingested\n49\t          * from outside the harness, which carries no `compiler.time.profiled`.\n50\t          */\n51\t        def warmupRamp: Maybe[Double] =\n52\t            if iterations.size < 3 then Maybe.empty\n53\t            else\n54\t                val rest   = iterations.tail.sorted\n55\t                val median = rest(rest.size / 2)\n56\t                if median <= 0.0 then Maybe.empty else Maybe(Math.abs(iterations.head - median) / median)\n57\t\n58\t        /** Whether the first iteration is an outlier against the spread of the remaining ones.\n59\t          *\n60\t          * A bare percentage cannot decide this: 5% is ordinary jitter on a noisy row and a serious\n61\t          * ramp on a stable one. The remaining iterations already say how much this row varies when\n62\t          * nothing is warming up, so the question is whether the first sits outside that, by a margin.\n63\t          *\n64\t          * The margin is a factor of two over the widest deviation among the rest, with a small\n65\t          * absolute floor so a perfectly stable row does not trip on rounding.\n66\t          */\n67\t        def startBias: Maybe[Double] =\n68\t            if iterations.size < 4 then Maybe.empty\n69\t            else\n70\t                val rest     = iterations.tail\n71\t                val restMean = rest.sum / rest.size\n72\t                // measured against this row's OWN iterations, never against `score`. A delta from a\n73\t                // replicated bracket carries the mean across legs in `score`, so comparing it to one\n74\t                // leg's iterations measures the gap between legs and calls it a warmup ramp. That\n75\t                // misfired on 26.5, 27.3, 27.2, 27.3, 27.2, a series whose own mean is stable.\n76\t                val allMean = iterations.sum / iterations.size\n77\t                if restMean <= 0.0 then Maybe.empty\n78\t                else Maybe((allMean - restMean) / restMean)\n79\t\n80\t        /** Whether the first iteration both stands out from the rest and moves the reported score.\n81\t          *\n82\t          * Two earlier criteria were tried against real data and both failed. \"First iteration more\n83\t          * than N% from the median\" cannot work with a fixed N: 5% is jitter on a noisy row and a\n84\t          * serious ramp on a stable one. \"First iteration is an outlier against the rest's spread\"\n85\t          * fails differently: two real rows tripped it at 2.43x and 2.53x, one a genuine ramp and one\n86\t          * a 0.53us row whose absolute jitter is negligible.\n87\t          *\n88\t          * What separates them is the quantity with consequences: how far the first iteration drags\n89\t          * the mean the verdict is computed from. On those two rows that is 1.64% against 0.59%.\n90\t          * Outlier status still has to hold, so ordinary noise in a single direction does not qualify.\n91\t          */\n92\t        def unsettledStart: Boolean =\n93\t            if iterations.size < 4 then false\n94\t            else\n95\t                val rest   = iterations.tail\n96\t                val sorted = rest.sorted\n97\t                val median = sorted(sorted.size / 2)\n98\t                if median <= 0.0 then false\n99\t                else\n100\t                    val spread   = rest.map(x => Math.abs(x - median)).max\n101\t                    val first    = Math.abs(iterations.head - median)\n102\t                    val isOutlier = first > 2.0 * spread\n103\t                    isOutlier && startBias.exists(b => Math.abs(b) > 0.01)\n104\t    end Row\n105\t\n106\t    /** One inlining decision at one call site, as the JIT reported it. The byte count is the part that matters: it is what turns a delivery\n107\t      * path from always-inlined into never-inlined, and it is invisible to every other tool.\n108\t      *\n109\t      * This is a *site* record, never a method's verdict. The distinction is load-bearing: see `InlineSites`.\n110\t      */\n111\t    case class JitEntry(method: String, bytes: Int, inlined: Boolean, reason: String) derives Schema\n112\t\n113\t    /** Every inlining decision the JIT made about one method, kept per site.\n114\t      *\n115\t      * Folding a method's sites to a single worst verdict is what let one warmup-era refusal, at one site out of six, decide the method's\n116\t      * verdict for a whole leg. Two runs of an identical comparison named disjoint mechanisms that way, one of them a 2-byte method\n117\t      * \"refused\" for size. A verdict is only meaningful with its denominator, so the denominator is carried.\n118\t      */\n119\t    case class InlineSites(method: String, bytes: Int, inlined: Int, refused: Int, reasons: Chunk[String]) derives Schema:\n120\t        def sites: Int = inlined + refused\n121\t\n122\t        /** True when the JIT refused at every site. Anything short of that is a mixed verdict and is reported as a fraction. */\n123\t        def alwaysRefused: Boolean = inlined == 0 && refused > 0\n124\t\n125\t        /** True when the JIT inlined at every site. */\n126\t        def alwaysInlined: Boolean = refused == 0 && inlined > 0\n127\t\n128\t        def show: String =\n129\t            if alwaysInlined then s\"${bytes}B inlined\"\n130\t            else if alwaysRefused then s\"${bytes}B refused (${reasons.headMaybe.getOrElse(\"no reason\")})\"\n131\t            else s\"${bytes}B refused at $refused/$sites sites (${reasons.headMaybe.getOrElse(\"no reason\")})\"\n132\t\n133\t        /** Whether this method is refused for size while sitting close enough to a budget that shrinking it could plausibly flip the verdict.\n134\t          *\n135\t          * The distinction a bare refusal list cannot make: a 379-byte body refused against a 325-byte budget is one edit away from\n136\t          * inlining, and a 4000-byte one is furniture. That 379-byte case was the whole mechanism behind a regression this harness had failed\n137\t          * to explain for two sessions, and finding it took a manual read of the log because nothing here ranked refusals this way.\n138\t          *\n139\t          * Within twice the budget is the window: far enough to catch a method that needs real work, near enough to exclude the hopeless.\n140\t          */\n141\t        def nearBudget: Maybe[String] =\n142\t            val sizeRefusal = reasons.exists(r => r.contains(\"too big\") || r.contains(\"too large\"))\n143\t            if !sizeRefusal || refused == 0 then Maybe.empty\n144\t            else\n145\t                val budgets = Seq(35 -> \"MaxInlineSize\", 325 -> \"FreqInlineSize\")\n146\t                Maybe.fromOption(\n147\t                    budgets.collectFirst {\n148\t                        case (limit, name) if bytes > limit && bytes <= limit * 2 =>\n149\t                            f\"${bytes}B against $name ($limit), ${bytes.toDouble / limit}%.2fx over\"\n150\t                    }\n151\t                )\n152\t    end InlineSites\n153\t\n154\t    /** One method's inlining verdict moving between two runs of the same sources under different conditions.\n155\t      *\n156\t      * Proving that a JVM flag actually took effect requires exactly this and nothing more. Without it the efficacy gate, which is the step\n157\t      * that separates a measured mechanism from a confident story, is a manual diff of two logs and therefore in practice optional.\n158\t      */\n159\t    case class VerdictChange(method: String, bytes: Int, before: InlineSites, after: InlineSites) derives Schema:\n160\t        def show: String = s\"$method: ${before.inlined}ok/${before.refused}fail -> ${after.inlined}ok/${after.refused}fail\"\n161\t\n162\t    /** How much of an artifact a parser actually consumed.\n163\t      *\n164\t      * A parser that reads 637 of 5093 elements and reports what it found looks identical to one that read all of them. Carrying the\n165\t      * fraction turns a silent partial parse into a visible one, and lets a test fail when the fraction drops.\n166\t      */\n167\t    case class ParseCoverage(what: String, seen: Int, parsed: Int) derives Schema:\n168\t        def complete: Boolean = seen == parsed\n169\t        def show: String      = if complete then s\"$what $parsed/$seen\" else s\"$what $parsed/$seen (INCOMPLETE)\"\n170\t\n171\t    /** Bytes allocated by one class, as the allocation profiler attributed them.\n172\t      *\n173\t      * `samples` is carried alongside `bytes` because it is the only currency the two allocation\n174\t      * views share: the flat table reports both, the collapsed view reports samples only, and a\n175\t      * conservation check between them has to compare like with like.\n176\t      */\n177\t    case class AllocSite(cls: String, bytes: Long, samples: Long = 0L) derives Schema\n178\t\n179\t    /** Which method allocated a class, from the collapsed (FlameGraph folded) view.\n180\t      *\n181\t      * The flat table answers *what* was allocated and never *by whom*: four classes and four byte\n182\t      * totals say nothing about which of the twenty call sites produced them. The collapsed view\n183\t      * carries the whole stack per sample, so the allocating frame is recoverable, and that is the\n184\t      * difference between \"Nested is half the allocation\" and \"half the allocation is Nested, minted\n185\t      * at this one site\".\n186\t      *\n187\t      * Its value is a sample count, never bytes: the collapsed dump JMH issues carries no `total`\n188\t      * option. `bytes` here is therefore apportioned from the flat table's byte figure for the same\n189\t      * class, in proportion to samples, and is labelled an estimate everywhere it is shown.\n190\t      *\n191\t      * The confound that cannot be removed: with inlining, the frame the profiler names is where the\n192\t      * JIT *placed* the allocation, not where the source wrote it. An inlining change relocates this\n193\t      * attribution without anything about the allocation changing, so a per-method allocation\n194\t      * mechanism is never independent of the inlining mechanism, and the report says so.\n195\t      */\n196\t    case class AllocByMethod(\n197\t        cls: String,\n198\t        /** The frame the allocation happened in, which is often the type's own factory. */\n199\t        method: String,\n200\t        samples: Long,\n201\t        bytes: Maybe[Double] = Maybe.empty,\n202\t        /** The first frame in the stack that is not the allocated type's own code.\n203\t          *\n204\t          * The immediate frame is frequently useless on its own: every `Nested` on\n205\t          * `nestedPayloadsUnwrapInMaps` is minted at `Nested$.apply`, which is true, unsurprising, and\n206\t          * decides nothing. One frame further out is `ProtoKernelBench$.boxed`, and that is the\n207\t          * answer to the question anyone is actually asking, which is who asked for the allocation.\n208\t          */\n209\t        site: String = \"\"\n210\t    ) derives Schema:\n211\t        def show: String =\n212\t            val b = bytes.map(x => f\", ~${x}%.0f B\").getOrElse(\"\")\n213\t            val where = if site.isEmpty || site == method then method else s\"$method, called from $site\"\n214\t            s\"$cls minted at $where ($samples samples$b)\"\n215\t\n216\t    /** A sampled method and the nanoseconds attributed to it. */\n217\t    case class CpuSite(method: String, nanos: Long) derives Schema\n218\t\n219\t    /** What compiling this leg cost, and whether it finished in time.\n220\t      *\n221\t      * Collected because a design that takes materially longer to reach steady state is telling you something: bigger methods, more\n222\t      * recompilation, or an unstable profile that keeps deoptimising. Treating that as noise to warm past would discard the finding.\n223\t      */\n224\t    case class JitMetrics(\n225\t        /** Milliseconds compiling during the measured window. Above the threshold the score is a mixture, not a steady state. */\n226\t        msInWindow: Double,\n227\t        /** Milliseconds compiling over the whole fork. */\n228\t        msTotal: Double,\n229\t        tasks: Int,\n230\t        c2Tasks: Int,\n231\t        /** Tasks compiling a loop that was already running. The JMH stub loop is one of these, and it is where the measured code actually\n232\t          * runs, so folding them into `tasks` hides the compilation that matters most.\n233\t          */\n234\t        osrTasks: Int,\n235\t        recompiled: Int,\n236\t        /** Deoptimizations that actually happened: `<uncommon_trap thread=...>`, emitted when a running method falls back to the\n237\t          * interpreter. In a captured run there were 6 of these.\n238\t          */\n239\t        runtimeDeopts: Int,\n240\t        /** Guards the compiler planted while compiling (`bci=`), a property of the code shape rather than an event. There were 633 in the\n241\t          * same run, and summing them with the above produced a \"deoptimizations 642 vs 645\" row that compared guard censuses.\n242\t          */\n243\t        plantedTraps: Int,\n244\t        /** Compiled methods invalidated and scheduled for recompilation. The real recompilation signal, and previously unparsed. */\n245\t        madeNotEntrant: Int,\n246\t        /** Seconds from JVM start to the last compilation. Compare against when measurement began. */\n247\t        lastCompileAt: Double\n248\t    ) derives Schema\n249\t\n250\t    /** A deoptimization reason and how often it fired.\n251\t      *\n252\t      * Invisible to every other tool here. A method whose profile went unstable falls back to the interpreter and is recompiled, which is a\n253\t      * real cost that no timing or allocation figure explains.\n254\t      */\n255\t    case class Deopt(reason: String, count: Int) derives Schema\n256\t\n257\t    /** A call site's receiver profile, aggregated by callee.\n258\t      *\n259\t      * `monomorphic` is `Absent` when the log carries no receiver profile for the site, which is the common case by a wide margin: 12 of\n260\t      * 5093 call elements in a captured run have one. Absence means the JIT never profiled the site as a virtual call, typically because it\n261\t      * was statically bound or already devirtualized. It emphatically does not mean megamorphic.\n262\t      *\n263\t      * Encoding that as `Maybe` rather than `false` is the whole point. With a boolean, \"no data\" and \"many receivers\" are the same value,\n264\t      * and a report printed 46 of 47 sites under a heading promising measured receiver counts when every one of them had a receiver count of\n265\t      * zero. A site with no profile is now unrepresentable as a classification.\n266\t      */\n267\t    case class CallMorphism(callee: String, count: Long, receiverCount: Long, monomorphic: Maybe[Boolean]) derives Schema:\n268\t        /** Sites the JIT actually profiled, the only ones anything may be said about. */\n269\t        def profiled: Boolean = monomorphic.isDefined\n270\t\n271\t    /** A source pattern whose occurrence count identifies which design a tree held. */\n272\t    case class Marker(name: String, count: Int) derives Schema\n273\t\n274\t    /** The machine and session a run belongs to.\n275\t      *\n276\t      * Comparing runs across sessions is the mistake that made a row look 3.6% slower when back-to-back it was parity, so the session is\n277\t      * carried on every run and checked at comparison time. `driftPercent` is measured by running the control twice at session start rather\n278\t      * than assumed, which is what lets a verdict be classified against this machine's actual noise floor.\n279\t      */\n280\t    case class Session(id: String, host: String, jvm: String, driftPercent: Double) derives Schema\n281\t\n282\t    /** Everything one leg produced, with the provenance needed to trust it. */\n283\t    case class Run(\n284\t        id: String,\n285\t        session: Session,\n286\t        label: String,\n287\t        sha: String,\n288\t        /** Hash of the measured sources, sampled before and after the leg: a change mid-run invalidates it. */\n289\t        treeHash: String,\n290\t        forks: Int,\n291\t        evidence: Evidence,\n292\t        wholeClass: Boolean,\n293\t        declaredRows: Int,\n294\t        markers: Chunk[Marker],\n295\t        /** False when the measured window still contained meaningful compilation. A comparison built from such a leg cannot be trusted, so\n296\t          * the fact travels with the record rather than living only in a printed line.\n297\t          */\n298\t        /** Warmup iterations used. Fixed per session so legs are comparable, never silently escalated. */\n299\t        warmup: Int,\n300\t        jit_metrics: Maybe[JitMetrics],\n301\t        rows: Chunk[Row],\n302\t        /** Inlining decisions per method, with every site kept. Sourced from the compilation log, which supersedes `PrintInlining`\n303\t          * entirely: that tool interleaves output across compiler threads and reports no denominator.\n304\t          */\n305\t        jit: Chunk[InlineSites],\n306\t        /** How much of each parsed artifact was actually consumed, so a silent partial parse is visible in the record. */\n307\t        coverage: Chunk[ParseCoverage],\n308\t        /** The extra JVM arguments this leg was measured under.\n309\t          *\n310\t          * A configuration comparison varies nothing but these, so a stored pair with the same `sha`\n311\t          * and the same `treeHash` is otherwise indistinguishable, and the campaign's headline result\n312\t          * was stored exactly that way: `continuationBodiesFuse` at -6.8% under a forced inline, with\n313\t          * the forcing recorded nowhere. The run could be read, re-compared and re-reported, and no\n314\t          * reader could say what it had measured.\n315\t          */\n316\t        jvmArgs: Chunk[String] = Chunk.empty,\n317\t        alloc: Chunk[AllocSite],\n318\t        /** Who allocated each class, from the collapsed view of the same recording.\n319\t          *\n320\t          * Defaulted, and that default is load-bearing rather than a convenience: adding this field\n321\t          * without one made every run already in the store undecodable, all 34 of them, with the\n322\t          * whole campaign's data behind them. A stored run is the durable record; a field added to\n323\t          * `Run` must leave the old ones readable, and `StoreSchemaTest` decodes a run recorded before\n324\t          * this field existed to keep that true.\n325\t          */\n326\t        allocByMethod: Chunk[AllocByMethod] = Chunk.empty,\n327\t        cpu: Chunk[CpuSite],\n328\t        deopts: Chunk[Deopt],\n329\t        morphism: Chunk[CallMorphism],\n330\t        recordedAt: String\n331\t    ) derives Schema:\n332\t        def row(name: String): Maybe[Row]              = Maybe.fromOption(rows.find(_.name == name))\n333\t        def jitFor(method: String): Maybe[InlineSites] = Maybe.fromOption(jit.find(_.method == method))\n334\t    end Run\n335\t\n336\t    enum Verdict derives Schema, CanEqual:\n337\t        case Faster, Flat, Regressed, BelowResolution\n338\t\n339\t    /** How small an effect this row could have detected, and on what basis.\n340\t      *\n341\t      * Carried on every delta, including flat ones. \"Flat\" without a resolution is not a result: it is indistinguishable from an instrument\n342\t      * that cannot see anything, and a harness unable to say how small an effect it would have caught is not entitled to call a row\n343\t      * unchanged.\n344\t      */\n345\t    case class Resolution(percent: Double, absolute: Double, df: Int, alpha: Double) derives Schema:\n346\t        def show: String = f\"detectable at +-${percent}%.2f%% (df=$df, alpha=$alpha%.5f)\"\n347\t\n348\t    /** A row's movement between two runs, together with whether anything in the evidence moved with it.\n349\t      *\n350\t      * `mechanism` is the point of the whole harness: a timing change with no allocation change, no inlining change and no shift in the\n351\t      * sampled profile is either noise or an unexplained mechanism. Saying which is not the tool's job, but refusing to let the reader\n352\t      * assume one was found is.\n353\t      */\n354\t    case class Delta(\n355\t        row: String,\n356\t        control: Row,\n357\t        variant: Row,\n358\t        percent: Double,\n359\t        verdict: Verdict,\n360\t        allocDelta: Maybe[Double],\n361\t        mechanism: Chunk[String],\n362\t        /** Present when the session replicated its legs. Absent means the verdict rests on a single pair, which cannot support a threshold. */\n363\t        resolution: Maybe[Resolution] = Maybe.empty\n364\t    ) derives Schema:\n365\t        def unexplained: Boolean = verdict != Verdict.Flat && verdict != Verdict.BelowResolution && mechanism.isEmpty\n366\t\n367\t        /** A flat row with no resolution is not evidence of no change; it is evidence of nothing. */\n368\t        def flatButUnbounded: Boolean = verdict == Verdict.Flat && resolution.isEmpty\n369\t    end Delta\n370\t\n371\t    case class Comparison(\n372\t        control: Run,\n373\t        variant: Run,\n374\t        deltas: Chunk[Delta],\n375\t        jitChanges: Chunk[String]\n376\t    ) derives Schema\n377\t\n378\tend Model\n379\t"}]},"uuid":"9b7b163f-9f61-4f07-ada2-8dbf61c7a043","timestamp":"2026-08-17T16:05:36.006Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/effervescent-painting-backus/kyo-kernel2/.claude/skills/kernel/bench-harness/Model.scala","content":"import kyo.*\n\n/** What a run captured, and what a comparison of two runs concluded.\n  *\n  * Records are persisted as json and every comparison is a pure function over them, so re-reading what the JIT decided about a method, or\n  * re-deriving a verdict, never re-runs a benchmark and never varies between readings.\n  */\nobject Model:\n\n    /** How much of the evidence ladder a run collected. A comparison built from anything below `Full` cannot attribute a movement to a\n      * mechanism, and says so rather than leaving the reader to assume one was checked.\n      */\n    enum Evidence derives Schema, CanEqual:\n        case Timing, Full\n\n    /** One benchmark row: the score with its error, plus the allocation JMH's gc profiler attributes to it. */\n    case class Row(\n        name: String,\n        mode: String,\n        count: Int,\n        score: Double,\n        error: Double,\n        unit: String,\n        /** The per-iteration series JMH recorded, kept rather than reduced to a count.\n          *\n          * A summary score hides the shape that produced it. A real control leg read\n          * `[86.4, 80.8, 81.4, 78.5, 78.6]`: a warmup ramp whose first iteration inflated both the\n          * mean and the error, and which the harness could not see at all because it kept only the\n          * count. That leg then carried a -9.8% \"win\" that was substantially its own unsettled start.\n          */\n        iterations: Chunk[Double],\n        allocPerOp: Maybe[Double],\n        /** Milliseconds the JIT spent compiling *during the measured window*. Non-trivial values mean the JVM had not reached steady state\n          * and the score describes a mixture of compiled and compiling code.\n          */\n        compilerMsProfiled: Maybe[Double],\n        compilerMsTotal: Maybe[Double]\n    ) derives Schema:\n        /** Compilation during measurement as a fraction of the measured wall time. */\n        def compilingShare(measuredMs: Double): Maybe[Double] = compilerMsProfiled.map(_ / measuredMs * 100)\n\n        /** This row's own relative uncertainty, as a fraction of its score. */\n        def relativeError: Double = if score <= 0.0 then 0.0 else error / score\n\n        /** How far the first measured iteration sits from the median of the rest, as a fraction.\n          *\n          * A leg still warming up shows it here and nowhere else: the score and the error absorb the\n          * ramp without revealing it. This is the only steady-state signal available to a run ingested\n          * from outside the harness, which carries no `compiler.time.profiled`.\n          */\n        def warmupRamp: Maybe[Double] =\n            if iterations.size < 3 then Maybe.empty\n            else\n                val rest   = iterations.tail.sorted\n                val median = rest(rest.size / 2)\n                if median <= 0.0 then Maybe.empty else Maybe(Math.abs(iterations.head - median) / median)\n\n        /** Whether the first iteration is an outlier against the spread of the remaining ones.\n          *\n          * A bare percentage cannot decide this: 5% is ordinary jitter on a noisy row and a serious\n          * ramp on a stable one. The remaining iterations already say how much this row varies when\n          * nothing is warming up, so the question is whether the first sits outside that, by a margin.\n          *\n          * The margin is a factor of two over the widest deviation among the rest, with a small\n          * absolute floor so a perfectly stable row does not trip on rounding.\n          */\n        def startBias: Maybe[Double] =\n            if iterations.size < 4 then Maybe.empty\n            else\n                val rest     = iterations.tail\n                val restMean = rest.sum / rest.size\n                // measured against this row's OWN iterations, never against `score`. A delta from a\n                // replicated bracket carries the mean across legs in `score`, so comparing it to one\n                // leg's iterations measures the gap between legs and calls it a warmup ramp. That\n                // misfired on 26.5, 27.3, 27.2, 27.3, 27.2, a series whose own mean is stable.\n                val allMean = iterations.sum / iterations.size\n                if restMean <= 0.0 then Maybe.empty\n                else Maybe((allMean - restMean) / restMean)\n\n        /** Whether the first iteration both stands out from the rest and moves the reported score.\n          *\n          * Two earlier criteria were tried against real data and both failed. \"First iteration more\n          * than N% from the median\" cannot work with a fixed N: 5% is jitter on a noisy row and a\n          * serious ramp on a stable one. \"First iteration is an outlier against the rest's spread\"\n          * fails differently: two real rows tripped it at 2.43x and 2.53x, one a genuine ramp and one\n          * a 0.53us row whose absolute jitter is negligible.\n          *\n          * What separates them is the quantity with consequences: how far the first iteration drags\n          * the mean the verdict is computed from. On those two rows that is 1.64% against 0.59%.\n          * Outlier status still has to hold, so ordinary noise in a single direction does not qualify.\n          */\n        def unsettledStart: Boolean =\n            if iterations.size < 4 then false\n            else\n                val rest   = iterations.tail\n                val sorted = rest.sorted\n                val median = sorted(sorted.size / 2)\n                if median <= 0.0 then false\n                else\n                    val spread   = rest.map(x => Math.abs(x - median)).max\n                    val first    = Math.abs(iterations.head - median)\n                    val isOutlier = first > 2.0 * spread\n                    isOutlier && startBias.exists(b => Math.abs(b) > 0.01)\n    end Row\n\n    /** One inlining decision at one call site, as the JIT reported it. The byte count is the part that matters: it is what turns a delivery\n      * path from always-inlined into never-inlined, and it is invisible to every other tool.\n      *\n      * This is a *site* record, never a method's verdict. The distinction is load-bearing: see `InlineSites`.\n      */\n    case class JitEntry(method: String, bytes: Int, inlined: Boolean, reason: String) derives Schema\n\n    /** Every inlining decision the JIT made about one method, kept per site.\n      *\n      * Folding a method's sites to a single worst verdict is what let one warmup-era refusal, at one site out of six, decide the method's\n      * verdict for a whole leg. Two runs of an identical comparison named disjoint mechanisms that way, one of them a 2-byte method\n      * \"refused\" for size. A verdict is only meaningful with its denominator, so the denominator is carried.\n      */\n    case class InlineSites(method: String, bytes: Int, inlined: Int, refused: Int, reasons: Chunk[String]) derives Schema:\n        def sites: Int = inlined + refused\n\n        /** True when the JIT refused at every site. Anything short of that is a mixed verdict and is reported as a fraction. */\n        def alwaysRefused: Boolean = inlined == 0 && refused > 0\n\n        /** True when the JIT inlined at every site. */\n        def alwaysInlined: Boolean = refused == 0 && inlined > 0\n\n        def show: String =\n            if alwaysInlined then s\"${bytes}B inlined\"\n            else if alwaysRefused then s\"${bytes}B refused (${reasons.headMaybe.getOrElse(\"no reason\")})\"\n            else s\"${bytes}B refused at $refused/$sites sites (${reasons.headMaybe.getOrElse(\"no reason\")})\"\n\n        /** Whether this method is refused for size while sitting close enough to a budget that shrinking it could plausibly flip the verdict.\n          *\n          * The distinction a bare refusal list cannot make: a 379-byte body refused against a 325-byte budget is one edit away from\n          * inlining, and a 4000-byte one is furniture. That 379-byte case was the whole mechanism behind a regression this harness had failed\n          * to explain for two sessions, and finding it took a manual read of the log because nothing here ranked refusals this way.\n          *\n          * Within twice the budget is the window: far enough to catch a method that needs real work, near enough to exclude the hopeless.\n          */\n        def nearBudget: Maybe[String] =\n            val sizeRefusal = reasons.exists(r => r.contains(\"too big\") || r.contains(\"too large\"))\n            if !sizeRefusal || refused == 0 then Maybe.empty\n            else\n                val budgets = Seq(35 -> \"MaxInlineSize\", 325 -> \"FreqInlineSize\")\n                Maybe.fromOption(\n                    budgets.collectFirst {\n                        case (limit, name) if bytes > limit && bytes <= limit * 2 =>\n                            f\"${bytes}B against $name ($limit), ${bytes.toDouble / limit}%.2fx over\"\n                    }\n                )\n    end InlineSites\n\n    /** One method's inlining verdict moving between two runs of the same sources under different conditions.\n      *\n      * Proving that a JVM flag actually took effect requires exactly this and nothing more. Without it the efficacy gate, which is the step\n      * that separates a measured mechanism from a confident story, is a manual diff of two logs and therefore in practice optional.\n      */\n    case class VerdictChange(method: String, bytes: Int, before: InlineSites, after: InlineSites) derives Schema:\n        def show: String = s\"$method: ${before.inlined}ok/${before.refused}fail -> ${after.inlined}ok/${after.refused}fail\"\n\n    /** How much of an artifact a parser actually consumed.\n      *\n      * A parser that reads 637 of 5093 elements and reports what it found looks identical to one that read all of them. Carrying the\n      * fraction turns a silent partial parse into a visible one, and lets a test fail when the fraction drops.\n      */\n    case class ParseCoverage(what: String, seen: Int, parsed: Int) derives Schema:\n        def complete: Boolean = seen == parsed\n        def show: String      = if complete then s\"$what $parsed/$seen\" else s\"$what $parsed/$seen (INCOMPLETE)\"\n\n    /** Bytes allocated by one class, as the allocation profiler attributed them.\n      *\n      * `samples` is carried alongside `bytes` because it is the only currency the two allocation\n      * views share: the flat table reports both, the collapsed view reports samples only, and a\n      * conservation check between them has to compare like with like.\n      */\n    case class AllocSite(cls: String, bytes: Long, samples: Long = 0L) derives Schema\n\n    /** Which method allocated a class, from the collapsed (FlameGraph folded) view.\n      *\n      * The flat table answers *what* was allocated and never *by whom*: four classes and four byte\n      * totals say nothing about which of the twenty call sites produced them. The collapsed view\n      * carries the whole stack per sample, so the allocating frame is recoverable, and that is the\n      * difference between \"Nested is half the allocation\" and \"half the allocation is Nested, minted\n      * at this one site\".\n      *\n      * Its value is a sample count, never bytes: the collapsed dump JMH issues carries no `total`\n      * option. `bytes` here is therefore apportioned from the flat table's byte figure for the same\n      * class, in proportion to samples, and is labelled an estimate everywhere it is shown.\n      *\n      * The confound that cannot be removed: with inlining, the frame the profiler names is where the\n      * JIT *placed* the allocation, not where the source wrote it. An inlining change relocates this\n      * attribution without anything about the allocation changing, so a per-method allocation\n      * mechanism is never independent of the inlining mechanism, and the report says so.\n      */\n    case class AllocByMethod(\n        cls: String,\n        /** The frame the allocation happened in, which is often the type's own factory. */\n        method: String,\n        samples: Long,\n        bytes: Maybe[Double] = Maybe.empty,\n        /** The first frame in the stack that is not the allocated type's own code.\n          *\n          * The immediate frame is frequently useless on its own: every `Nested` on\n          * `nestedPayloadsUnwrapInMaps` is minted at `Nested$.apply`, which is true, unsurprising, and\n          * decides nothing. One frame further out is `ProtoKernelBench$.boxed`, and that is the\n          * answer to the question anyone is actually asking, which is who asked for the allocation.\n          */\n        site: String = \"\"\n    ) derives Schema:\n        def show: String =\n            val b = bytes.map(x => f\", ~${x}%.0f B\").getOrElse(\"\")\n            val where = if site.isEmpty || site == method then method else s\"$method, called from $site\"\n            s\"$cls minted at $where ($samples samples$b)\"\n\n    /** A sampled method and the nanoseconds attributed to it. */\n    case class CpuSite(method: String, nanos: Long) derives Schema\n\n    /** What compiling this leg cost, and whether it finished in time.\n      *\n      * Collected because a design that takes materially longer to reach steady state is telling you something: bigger methods, more\n      * recompilation, or an unstable profile that keeps deoptimising. Treating that as noise to warm past would discard the finding.\n      */\n    case class JitMetrics(\n        /** Milliseconds compiling during the measured window. Above the threshold the score is a mixture, not a steady state. */\n        msInWindow: Double,\n        /** Milliseconds compiling over the whole fork. */\n        msTotal: Double,\n        tasks: Int,\n        c2Tasks: Int,\n        /** Tasks compiling a loop that was already running. The JMH stub loop is one of these, and it is where the measured code actually\n          * runs, so folding them into `tasks` hides the compilation that matters most.\n          */\n        osrTasks: Int,\n        recompiled: Int,\n        /** Deoptimizations that actually happened: `<uncommon_trap thread=...>`, emitted when a running method falls back to the\n          * interpreter. In a captured run there were 6 of these.\n          */\n        runtimeDeopts: Int,\n        /** Guards the compiler planted while compiling (`bci=`), a property of the code shape rather than an event. There were 633 in the\n          * same run, and summing them with the above produced a \"deoptimizations 642 vs 645\" row that compared guard censuses.\n          */\n        plantedTraps: Int,\n        /** Compiled methods invalidated and scheduled for recompilation. The real recompilation signal, and previously unparsed. */\n        madeNotEntrant: Int,\n        /** Seconds from JVM start to the last compilation. Compare against when measurement began. */\n        lastCompileAt: Double\n    ) derives Schema\n\n    /** A deoptimization reason and how often it fired.\n      *\n      * Invisible to every other tool here. A method whose profile went unstable falls back to the interpreter and is recompiled, which is a\n      * real cost that no timing or allocation figure explains.\n      */\n    case class Deopt(reason: String, count: Int) derives Schema\n\n    /** A call site's receiver profile, aggregated by callee.\n      *\n      * `monomorphic` is `Absent` when the log carries no receiver profile for the site, which is the common case by a wide margin: 12 of\n      * 5093 call elements in a captured run have one. Absence means the JIT never profiled the site as a virtual call, typically because it\n      * was statically bound or already devirtualized. It emphatically does not mean megamorphic.\n      *\n      * Encoding that as `Maybe` rather than `false` is the whole point. With a boolean, \"no data\" and \"many receivers\" are the same value,\n      * and a report printed 46 of 47 sites under a heading promising measured receiver counts when every one of them had a receiver count of\n      * zero. A site with no profile is now unrepresentable as a classification.\n      */\n    case class CallMorphism(callee: String, count: Long, receiverCount: Long, monomorphic: Maybe[Boolean]) derives Schema:\n        /** Sites the JIT actually profiled, the only ones anything may be said about. */\n        def profiled: Boolean = monomorphic.isDefined\n\n    /** A source pattern whose occurrence count identifies which design a tree held. */\n    case class Marker(name: String, count: Int) derives Schema\n\n    /** The machine and session a run belongs to.\n      *\n      * Comparing runs across sessions is the mistake that made a row look 3.6% slower when back-to-back it was parity, so the session is\n      * carried on every run and checked at comparison time. `driftPercent` is measured by running the control twice at session start rather\n      * than assumed, which is what lets a verdict be classified against this machine's actual noise floor.\n      */\n    case class Session(id: String, host: String, jvm: String, driftPercent: Double) derives Schema\n\n    /** Everything one leg produced, with the provenance needed to trust it. */\n    case class Run(\n        id: String,\n        session: Session,\n        label: String,\n        sha: String,\n        /** Hash of the measured sources, sampled before and after the leg: a change mid-run invalidates it. */\n        treeHash: String,\n        forks: Int,\n        evidence: Evidence,\n        wholeClass: Boolean,\n        declaredRows: Int,\n        markers: Chunk[Marker],\n        /** False when the measured window still contained meaningful compilation. A comparison built from such a leg cannot be trusted, so\n          * the fact travels with the record rather than living only in a printed line.\n          */\n        /** Warmup iterations used. Fixed per session so legs are comparable, never silently escalated. */\n        warmup: Int,\n        jit_metrics: Maybe[JitMetrics],\n        rows: Chunk[Row],\n        /** Inlining decisions per method, with every site kept. Sourced from the compilation log, which supersedes `PrintInlining`\n          * entirely: that tool interleaves output across compiler threads and reports no denominator.\n          */\n        jit: Chunk[InlineSites],\n        /** How much of each parsed artifact was actually consumed, so a silent partial parse is visible in the record. */\n        coverage: Chunk[ParseCoverage],\n        /** The extra JVM arguments this leg was measured under.\n          *\n          * A configuration comparison varies nothing but these, so a stored pair with the same `sha`\n          * and the same `treeHash` is otherwise indistinguishable, and the campaign's headline result\n          * was stored exactly that way: `continuationBodiesFuse` at -6.8% under a forced inline, with\n          * the forcing recorded nowhere. The run could be read, re-compared and re-reported, and no\n          * reader could say what it had measured.\n          */\n        jvmArgs: Chunk[String] = Chunk.empty,\n        alloc: Chunk[AllocSite],\n        /** Who allocated each class, from the collapsed view of the same recording.\n          *\n          * Defaulted, and that default is load-bearing rather than a convenience: adding this field\n          * without one made every run already in the store undecodable, all 34 of them, with the\n          * whole campaign's data behind them. A stored run is the durable record; a field added to\n          * `Run` must leave the old ones readable, and `StoreSchemaTest` decodes a run recorded before\n          * this field existed to keep that true.\n          */\n        allocByMethod: Chunk[AllocByMethod] = Chunk.empty,\n        cpu: Chunk[CpuSite],\n        deopts: Chunk[Deopt],\n        morphism: Chunk[CallMorphism],\n        recordedAt: String\n    ) derives Schema:\n        def row(name: String): Maybe[Row]              = Maybe.fromOption(rows.find(_.name == name))\n        def jitFor(method: String): Maybe[InlineSites] = Maybe.fromOption(jit.find(_.method == method))\n    end Run\n\n    enum Verdict derives Schema, CanEqual:\n        case Faster, Flat, Regressed, BelowResolution\n\n    /** How small an effect this row could have detected, and on what basis.\n      *\n      * Carried on every delta, including flat ones. \"Flat\" without a resolution is not a result: it is indistinguishable from an instrument\n      * that cannot see anything, and a harness unable to say how small an effect it would have caught is not entitled to call a row\n      * unchanged.\n      */\n    case class Resolution(percent: Double, absolute: Double, df: Int, alpha: Double) derives Schema:\n        def show: String = f\"detectable at +-${percent}%.2f%% (df=$df, alpha=$alpha%.5f)\"\n\n    /** A row's movement between two runs, together with whether anything in the evidence moved with it.\n      *\n      * `mechanism` is the point of the whole harness: a timing change with no allocation change, no inlining change and no shift in the\n      * sampled profile is either noise or an unexplained mechanism. Saying which is not the tool's job, but refusing to let the reader\n      * assume one was found is.\n      */\n    case class Delta(\n        row: String,\n        control: Row,\n        variant: Row,\n        percent: Double,\n        verdict: Verdict,\n        allocDelta: Maybe[Double],\n        mechanism: Chunk[String],\n        /** Present when the session replicated its legs. Absent means the verdict rests on a single pair, which cannot support a threshold. */\n        resolution: Maybe[Resolution] = Maybe.empty\n    ) derives Schema:\n        def unexplained: Boolean = verdict != Verdict.Flat && verdict != Verdict.BelowResolution && mechanism.isEmpty\n\n        /** A flat row with no resolution is not evidence of no change; it is evidence of nothing. */\n        def flatButUnbounded: Boolean = verdict == Verdict.Flat && resolution.isEmpty\n    end Delta\n\n    case class Comparison(\n        control: Run,\n        variant: Run,\n        deltas: Chunk[Delta],\n        jitChanges: Chunk[String]\n    ) derives Schema\n\nend Model\n","numLines":379,"startLine":1,"totalLines":379}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f363ab96-0619-49cf-9551-3ad235db98bf","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}
