Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"run $id is unreadable: $other\"))\n25\t                }\n26\t            // the raw FileNotFoundException names a path the operator never typed and says nothing\n27\t            // about what they could have typed instead. `bench list` is one command away, so the\n28\t            // failure runs it for them.\n29\t            case false =>\n30\t                ids(root).map { known =>\n31\t                    Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(\n32\t                        s\"no run '$id' in store $root\" +\n33\t                            (if known.isEmpty then \", which holds no runs\"\n34\t                             else s\". It holds ${known.size}:\\n\" + known.map(k => s\"  $k\").mkString(\"\\n\"))\n35\t                    ))\n36\t                }\n37\t        }\n38\t    end load\n39\t\n40\t    /** The run ids a store holds, without decoding any of them. */\n41\t    def ids(root: Path)(using Frame): Chunk[String] < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException | Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n42\t        requireStore(root).andThen(\n43\t            dir(root).list.map(_.flatMap(f => Chunk.from(f.name.filter(_.endsWith(\".json\")).map(_.dropRight(5)))).sorted)\n44\t        )\n45\t\n46\t    /** Fails when the store is not there at all.\n47\t      *\n48\t      * A missing store used to read as an empty one: `bench list --store <typo>` printed \"no runs\n49\t      * stored\" and exited 0, so a mistyped path was indistinguishable from a store whose runs really\n50\t      * were gone. That is the shape of failure this whole harness exists to refuse, arriving through\n51\t      * its own front door.\n52\t      */\n53\t    def requireStore(root: Path)(using Frame): Unit < (Sync & Abort[Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n54\t        dir(root).exists.map { ok =>\n55\t            Abort.when(!ok)(Bench.BracketFailed(\n56\t                s\"no store at $root (there is no ${dir(root).name.getOrElse(\"runs\")}/ directory under it). \" +\n57\t                    \"A store is created by `run` or `bracket`; if you expected runs here, the path is wrong.\"\n58\t            ))\n59\t        }\n60\t\n61\t    def list(root: Path)(using Frame): Chunk[Run] < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException | FileReadException | Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n62\t        requireStore(root).andThen {\n63\t            dir(root).list.map { files =>\n64\t                Kyo.foreach(files.filter(_.name.exists(_.endsWith(\".json\")))) { f =>\n65\t                    f.read.map { raw =>\n66\t                        Json.decode[Run](raw) match\n67\t                            case Result.Success(r) => r\n68\t                            case other             => Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${f.name} is unreadable: $other\"))\n69\t                    }\n70\t                }\n71\t            }\n72\t        }\n73\t\n74\t    /** Recovers a session from any run that recorded it, so later legs join the same one. */\n75\t    def session(root: Path, id: String)(using Frame): Session < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException | FileReadException | Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n76\t        list(root).map { runs =>\n77\t            runs.find(_.session.id == id) match\n78\t                case Some(r) => r.session\n79\t                case None    => Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"no stored run belongs to session $id\"))\n80\t        }\n81\t\n82\tend Store\n83\t\n84\t/** Renders a comparison.\n85\t  *\n86\t  * The rules the skill states are enforced here rather than remembered: a verdict about the whole class is unreachable from a subset run, a\n87\t  * movement with nothing in the evidence behind it is labelled unexplained rather than narrated, and a run that skipped the ladder cannot\n88\t  * present itself as attributed.\n89\t  */\n90\tobject Report:\n91\t\n92\t    /** Conditions under which the numbers below are not readable, whatever they say.\n93\t      *\n94\t      * Both members are the same failure: a score that mixes warm and cold code. They were previously\n95\t      * a warning line each, one in the middle of the report and one near the end, which is a placement\n96\t      * that assumes the reader is disciplined. The operator this tool exists for is demonstrably not,\n97\t      * and glanced past exactly such a line on a leg whose first iteration was an outlier.\n98\t      *\n99\t      * So they become blockers: rendered first, under a banner, and the process exits non-zero. The\n100\t      * data is still printed in full, because suppressing it would trade one silent failure for\n101\t      * another; what changes is that the run cannot be mistaken for a clean one.\n102\t      */\n103\t    def blockers(c: Comparison): Chunk[String] =\n104\t        val unsettled =\n105\t            c.deltas.flatMap { d =>\n106\t                Chunk.from(Seq(\n107\t                    Option.when(d.control.unsettledStart)(s\"${d.row} (control) never settled: iterations ${d.control.iterations.map(x => f\"$x%.1f\").mkString(\", \")}\"),\n108\t                    Option.when(d.variant.unsettledStart)(s\"${d.row} (variant) never settled: iterations ${d.variant.iterations.map(x => f\"$x%.1f\").mkString(\", \")}\")\n109\t                ).flatten)\n110\t            }\n111\t        val compiling =\n112\t            Chunk.from(\n113\t                (Bench.stillCompiling(c.control).map((r, p) => f\"$r%s (control) spent ${p}%.1f%% of its measured window compiling\") ++\n114\t                    Bench.stillCompiling(c.variant).map((r, p) => f\"$r%s (variant) spent ${p}%.1f%% of its measured window compiling\"))\n115\t            )\n116\t        unsettled ++ compiling\n117\t    end blockers\n118\t\n119\t    /** What the A/A null establishes, and what it refuses.\n120\t      *\n121\t      * The null compares control legs against each other, so every row it classifies is a false\n122\t      * positive by construction. That makes a dirty null the strongest possible statement that the\n123\t      * session below is unreadable, and it was reported as a line of text that let the process exit 0.\n124\t      * The unsettled-leg finding is the same shape and was already fixed this way: a reader who skims\n125\t      * a thirty-line report skims a warning inside it, so this is a blocker with an exit code.\n126\t      *\n127\t      * A session with too few control legs to run a null at all is also a blocker, and for a stronger\n128\t      * reason: it is not that the check failed, it is that the session cannot check itself.\n129\t      */\n130\t    def nullBlockers(null_ : Maybe[Comparison], controlLegs: Int): Chunk[String] =\n131\t        null_ match\n132\t            case Maybe.Present(n) =>\n133\t                val named = n.deltas.filter(_.verdict != Verdict.Flat)\n134\t                if named.isEmpty then Chunk.empty\n135\t                else\n136\t                    Chunk(\n137\t                        s\"the A/A null classified ${named.size} row(s) comparing control legs against each other: \" +\n138\t                            named.map(d => f\"${d.row} ${d.percent}%+.1f%% (${d.verdict})\").mkString(\", \") +\n139\t                            \". Those verdicts are false by construction, so nothing below is readable.\"\n140\t                    )\n141\t            case _ =>\n142\t                Chunk(\n143\t                    s\"$controlLegs control leg(s) is too few to run an A/A null, so this session cannot check itself. \" +\n144\t                        \"Five legs gives three controls and is what the threshold below assumes.\"\n145\t                )\n146\t\n147\t    def nullNote(null_ : Maybe[Comparison]): String =\n148\t        null_ match\n149\t            case Maybe.Present(n) if n.deltas.forall(_.verdict == Verdict.Flat) =>\n150\t                f\"A/A null: clean, no control row classified against another control leg (${n.deltas.size} rows).\\n\"\n151\t            case _ => \"\"\n152\t\n153\t    /** What a two-sha comparison is structurally unable to say.\n154\t      *\n155\t      * A comparison of two commits measures the difference between two trees. Any statement of the\n156\t      * form \"this row moved *because of* change X\" additionally requires that X was isolated, and two\n157\t      * shas do not carry that: the partition between the changes inside the diff was never declared,\n158\t      * so the harness has nothing to attribute to.\n159\t      *\n160\t      * This is the failure the skill records as its worked example. Two changes shipped together, a\n161\t      * node-layout change and a currency hoist; the bundle was faster and the win was confidently\n162\t      * attributed first to one and then to the other, and both stories were wrong as told. What\n163\t      * settled it was running the pieces separately, which is a chain of shas rather than a pair.\n164\t      *\n165\t      * A configuration comparison, the same sha under two sets of JVM args, has nothing to partition\n166\t      * and gets no note.\n167\t      */\n168\t    def partitionNote(control: Run, variant: Run, chainLength: Int): String =\n169\t        if control.sha == variant.sha then\n170\t            // a configuration comparison varies nothing but the JVM arguments, so those ARE the\n171\t            // change under test and the report is the only place a reader can see them. The\n172\t            // campaign's headline was stored without them and could be re-read forever without\n173\t            // anyone being able to say what it had measured.\n174\t            val diff = variant.jvmArgs.diff(control.jvmArgs) ++ control.jvmArgs.diff(variant.jvmArgs)\n175\t            if diff.isEmpty then\n176\t                if control.jvmArgs.isEmpty && variant.jvmArgs.isEmpty then\n177\t                    \"\\n⚠️  Same sha and no recorded JVM arguments on either leg, so nothing here says \" +\n178\t                        \"what was varied. Either this is an A/A, or it was measured before the harness \" +\n179\t                        \"recorded configuration and the difference is unrecoverable.\"\n180\t                else \"\"\n181\t            else\n182\t                s\"\\nSame sha, so this is a configuration comparison and the difference is exactly:\\n\" +\n183\t                    diff.map(a => s\"  $a\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n184\t        else if chainLength > 2 then\n185\t            s\"\\nThis is one step of a $chainLength-sha chain, so the delta above is the isolated contribution of \" +\n186\t                \"this step and nothing else moved with it.\"\n187\t        else\n188\t            \"\\n⚠️  Two shas, so no source-level mechanism is attributable from this comparison. The diff \" +\n189\t                \"between them may contain any number of changes and the partition between them was never declared, \" +\n190\t                \"so a sentence of the form 'this moved because of change X' is not supported by anything here, \" +\n191\t                \"however plausible X is. Declare a chain of shas to isolate one.\"\n192\t\n193\t    /** A score rendered so its own digits survive.\n194\t      *\n195\t      * Two fixed decimals was the previous format and it hid the numbers behind a verdict. The row\n196\t      * `evalFixedOverhead` measures a few nanoseconds, so a real and cleanly separated regression\n197\t      * printed as `0.01 ± 0.00` against `0.01 ± 0.00` beside a `+26.2%`, with the error column reading\n198\t      * as though there were no error at all. The actual values were 0.005853 and 0.007364, which any\n199\t      * reader could have judged on sight.\n200\t      *\n201\t      * The skill requires that a reader can judge a result without asking what was measured or how\n202\t      * confident it is, and requires the error column specifically because a delta smaller than the\n203\t      * combined error is not a result. A format that rounds both to zero defeats both rules at once.\n204\t      */\n205\t    def score(x: Double): String =\n206\t        val a = Math.abs(x)\n207\t        if a == 0.0 then \"0\"\n208\t        else if a >= 100 then f\"$x%.1f\"\n209\t        else if a >= 1 then f\"$x%.2f\"\n210\t        else if a >= 0.01 then f\"$x%.4f\"\n211\t        else f\"$x%.6f\"\n212\t\n213\t    def icon(v: Verdict): String =\n214\t        v match\n215\t            case Verdict.Faster          => \"🟢\"\n216\t            case Verdict.Flat            => \"⚪\"\n217\t            case Verdict.Regressed       => \"🔴\"\n218\t            case Verdict.BelowResolution => \"🔵\"\n219\t\n220\t    def render(c: Comparison, chainLength: Int = 2): String =\n221\t        val control = c.control\n222\t        val variant = c.variant\n223\t        val scope =\n224\t            if control.wholeClass && variant.wholeClass then s\"all ${control.declaredRows} rows\"\n225\t            else s\"${c.deltas.size} selected rows of ${control.declaredRows}, so this says nothing about the rest\"\n226\t        val evidence =\n227\t            if control.evidence == Evidence.Full && variant.evidence == Evidence.Full then \"full ladder\"\n228\t            else \"timing only, so no movement here is attributed\"\n229\t        val forksNote = if variant.forks < 3 then s\", -f ${variant.forks} is diagnostic and not a claim\" else \"\"\n230\t        val drift     = Bench.band(control, variant)\n231\t        val bandNote =\n232\t            if control.session.driftPercent > 0 then f\"drift $drift%.1f%% measured this session\"\n233\t            else f\"drift $drift%.1f%% assumed, not measured\"\n234\t\n235\t        val header =\n236\t            s\"\"\"|Control `${control.sha.take(10)}` (${control.label}) against variant `${variant.sha.take(10)}` (${variant.label}).\n237\t                |JMH -f ${variant.forks}$forksNote, $scope, $evidence, $bandNote.\n238\t                |Markers control ${control.markers.map(m => s\"${m.name}=${m.count}\").mkString(\" \")} | variant ${variant.markers.map(m => s\"${m.name}=${m.count}\").mkString(\" \")}\n239\t                |\n240\t                || | row | mode | cnt | control | variant | delta | resolves | B/op delta | mechanism |\n241\t                ||---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\"\"\".stripMargin\n242\t\n243\t        // a leg whose first measured iteration sits far from the rest was still warming up, and its\n244\t        // score and error both absorb that without showing it. Only the per-iteration series reveals\n245\t        // it, and for an ingested run it is the only steady-state signal that exists at all.\n246\t        val RampLimit = 0.05\n247\t        val ramped =\n248\t            c.deltas.flatMap { d =>\n249\t                Chunk.from(Seq(\n250\t                    d.control.warmupRamp.filter(_ > RampLimit).map(r => (d.row, \"control\", r)),\n251\t                    d.variant.warmupRamp.filter(_ > RampLimit).map(r => (d.row, \"variant\", r))\n252\t                ).flatMap(_.toOption))\n253\t            }\n254\t        val rampNote =\n255\t            if ramped.isEmpty then \"\"\n256\t            else\n257\t                \"\\n\\u26a0\\ufe0f  A leg's first measured iteration sits far from the rest, so it was still warming up and \" +\n258\t                    \"its score includes that ramp:\\n\" +\n259\t                    ramped.map((row, side, r) => f\"  - $row%s ($side%s) first iteration is ${r * 100}%.0f%% from the median of the rest\")\n260\t                        .mkString(\"\\n\")\n261\t\n262\t        val resolutionNote =\n263\t            val unbounded = c.deltas.count(d => d.flatButUnbounded || d.verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution)\n264\t            val bounded   = c.deltas.flatMap(_.resolution)\n265\t            if bounded.nonEmpty then\n266\t                val worst = bounded.map(_.percent).max\n267\t                // df 0 marks a single-pair comparison: the bound is the legs' own reported error, not\n268\t                // a threshold estimated from replicates, and the two are not the same claim\n269\t                if bounded.head.df == 0 then\n270\t                    f\"\\nEvery flat row below is flat to within +-${worst}%.2f%%, the floor set by the legs' own reported \" +\n271\t                        \"error. These legs were not replicated, so this bounds the result without estimating the spread; \" +\n272\t                        \"a replicated bracket would give a real threshold and this does not.\"\n273\t                else\n274\t                    f\"\\nEvery flat row below is flat to within its own resolution, at worst +-${worst}%.2f%% \" +\n275\t                        f\"(alpha ${bounded.head.alpha}%.5f after correcting for ${c.deltas.size} rows, df ${bounded.head.df}).\"\n276\t            else if unbounded > 0 then\n277\t                s\"\\n⚠️  $unbounded flat rows carry no resolution: these legs were not replicated, so \" +\n278\t                    \"'flat' here means the harness cannot say how small an effect it would have missed, not that nothing changed.\"\n279\t            else \"\"\n280\t\n281\t        val body = c.deltas.map { d =>\n282\t            val delta = if d.verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution then \"below resolution\" else f\"${d.percent}%+.1f%%\"\n283\t            // this row's OWN threshold, not the worst across the table. The footer reports only the\n284\t            // worst, which cannot answer the question a flat row actually raises: was it close to\n285\t            // resolving, or nowhere near? On the replicated sweep two rows at -12.5% and -10.7% came\n286\t            // back flat while a -7.1% row was a win, and the table gave no way to see why.\n287\t            val res = d.resolution.map(r => f\"±${r.percent}%.1f%%\").getOrElse(\"-\")\n288\t            val alloc = d.allocDelta.map(a => f\"$a%+.0f\").getOrElse(\"-\")\n289\t            val mech =\n290\t                if d.mechanism.nonEmpty then d.mechanism.mkString(\"; \")\n291\t                else if d.unexplained then \"**none found**\"\n292\t                else \"-\"\n293\t            f\"| ${icon(d.verdict)} | `${d.row}` | ${d.control.mode} | ${d.variant.count} | \" +\n294\t                s\"${score(d.control.score)} ± ${score(d.control.error)} | ${score(d.variant.score)} ± ${score(d.variant.error)} | $delta | $res | $alloc | $mech |\"\n295\t        }.mkString(\"\\n\")\n296\t\n297\t        val jit =\n298\t            if c.jitChanges.isEmpty then \"\"\n299\t            else \"\\nInlining changed:\\n\" + c.jitChanges.map(s => s\"  - $s\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n300\t\n301\t        val deoptShift =\n302\t            val cd = control.deopts.map(d => d.reason -> d.count).toMap\n303\t            val moved = variant.deopts.filter(d => Math.abs(d.count - cd.getOrElse(d.reason, 0)) > cd.getOrElse(d.reason, 0) / 4 + 5)\n304\t            if moved.isEmpty then \"\"\n305\t            else\n306\t                \"\\nDeoptimization changed, which no timing or allocation figure explains:\\n\" +\n307\t                    moved.map(d => s\"  - ${d.reason}: ${cd.getOrElse(d.reason, 0)} -> ${d.count}\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n308\t\n309\t        val steadyState =\n310\t            val cs = Bench.stillCompiling(control)\n311\t            val vs = Bench.stillCompiling(variant)\n312\t            if cs.isEmpty && vs.isEmpty then \"\"\n313\t            else\n314\t                \"\\n\\U0001f6d1 NOT STEADY STATE. These rows were still being compiled while they were measured, so the scores mix compiled \" +\n315\t                    \"and compiling code. Do not read the deltas above until this is diagnosed. Warming longer would hide it: a benchmark \" +\n316\t                    \"that needs unusual warmup is reporting something about the code under it.\\n\" +\n317\t                    (cs.map((r, p) => f\"  - control $r%s spent ${p}%.1f%% of its window compiling\") ++\n318\t                        vs.map((r, p) => f\"  - variant $r%s spent ${p}%.1f%% of its window compiling\")).mkString(\"\\n\") +\n319\t                    \"\\n  Start from the JIT metrics below: more tasks, more recompilation or more deopts on one leg is the cause, not noise.\"\n320\t\n321\t        val jitTable =\n322\t            (control.jit_metrics, variant.jit_metrics) match\n323\t                case (Maybe.Present(c), Maybe.Present(v)) =>\n324\t                    def row(n: String, a: Double, b: Double, unit: String = \"\") =\n325\t                        val d = if a == 0.0 then \"\" else f\" (${(b - a) / a * 100}%+.0f%%)\"\n326\t                        f\"| $n%-24s | $a%10.0f$unit | $b%10.0f$unit |$d |\"\n327\t                    \"\\n\\nJIT cost, which is a property of the design and not only of the run:\\n\" +\n328\t                        \"| metric | control | variant | |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n\" +\n329\t                        Seq(\n330\t                            row(\"compiling in window\", c.msInWindow, v.msInWindow, \"ms\"),\n331\t                            row(\"compiling total\", c.msTotal, v.msTotal, \"ms\"),\n332\t                            row(\"compilation tasks\", c.tasks.toDouble, v.tasks.toDouble),\n333\t                            row(\"C2 tasks\", c.c2Tasks.toDouble, v.c2Tasks.toDouble),\n334\t                            row(\"OSR tasks\", c.osrTasks.toDouble, v.osrTasks.toDouble),\n335\t                            row(\"methods recompiled\", c.recompiled.toDouble, v.recompiled.toDouble),\n336\t                            // runtime events only. The planted-guard census used to sit in this row\n337\t                            // and swamped it: 633 guards against 6 real deoptimizations.\n338\t                            row(\"runtime deopts\", c.runtimeDeopts.toDouble, v.runtimeDeopts.toDouble),\n339\t                            row(\"made not entrant\", c.madeNotEntrant.toDouble, v.madeNotEntrant.toDouble),\n340\t                            row(\"last compile at\", c.lastCompileAt, v.lastCompileAt, \"s\")\n341\t                        ).mkString(\"\\n\")\n342\t                case _ => \"\"\n343\t\n344\t        val polymorphic =\n345\t            // only sites the JIT actually profiled a receiver for. The previous version filtered on\n346\t            // `!monomorphic`, which included every unprofiled site, and printed 46 of 47 of them\n347\t            // under a heading promising measured receiver counts while each had a receiver count of\n348\t            // zero. Absence of a profile is not evidence of polymorphism.\n349\t            val poly = variant.morphism.filter(_.monomorphic.contains(false)).take(3)\n350\t            if poly.isEmpty then \"\"\n351\t            else\n352\t                \"\\nPolymorphic call sites, among the few the JIT profiled a receiver for:\\n\" +\n353\t                    poly.map(m => s\"  - ${m.callee} ${m.count} calls, ${m.receiverCount} to the top receiver\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n354\t\n355\t        // an allocation change is exact and per-operation, so it does not need the timing to resolve.\n356\t        // A row can be flat in time and still allocate 240,000 B/op more, and suppressing the\n357\t        // mechanism on flat rows hid exactly that: the only visible trace was a number in a column.\n358\t        val allocMoved =\n359\t            c.deltas.filter(d => d.verdict != Verdict.Regressed && d.allocDelta.exists(a => Math.abs(a) > 1.0))\n360\t        val allocNote =\n361\t            if allocMoved.isEmpty then \"\"\n362\t            else\n363\t                \"\\n\\u2139\\ufe0f  Allocation moved on rows whose timing did not resolve. Allocation is exact and per-operation, \" +\n364\t                    \"so this is a real change regardless of what the timing could or could not show:\\n\" +\n365\t                    allocMoved.map(d => f\"  - ${d.row}%s ${d.allocDelta.getOrElse(0.0)}%+.0f B/op, timing ${d.percent}%+.1f%% (${d.verdict})\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n366\t\n367\t        // which method minted the class whose bytes moved. The flat table can only say that `Nested`\n368\t        // is half the allocation; this says half the allocation is `Nested`, minted at one site.\n369\t        val allocSites =\n370\t            val before = control.allocByMethod.map(m => (m.cls, m.method) -> m).toMap\n371\t            val after  = variant.allocByMethod.map(m => (m.cls, m.method) -> m).toMap\n372\t            val moved =\n373\t                (before.keySet ++ after.keySet).toSeq.flatMap { k =>\n374\t                    val b = before.get(k).map(_.samples).getOrElse(0L)\n375\t                    val a = after.get(k).map(_.samples).getOrElse(0L)\n376\t                    // a quarter of the larger side, so ordinary sampling jitter does not fill the list\n377\t                    if Math.abs(a - b) * 4 > Math.max(a, b) then Seq((k, b, a)) else Nil\n378\t                }.sortBy((_, b, a) => -Math.abs(a - b)).take(6)\n379\t            if moved.isEmpty then \"\"\n380\t            else\n381\t                \"\\nAllocation moved at these sites, by sample count:\\n\" +\n382\t                    moved.map((k, b, a) => s\"  - ${k._1} at ${k._2}: $b -> $a\").mkString(\"\\n\") +\n383\t                    \"\\n  These are whole-leg figures, not per row, and the frame named is where the JIT *placed* the \" +\n384\t                    \"allocation. An inlining change relocates it with nothing about the allocation changing, so this \" +\n385\t                    \"is never independent of the inlining verdicts above.\"\n386\t\n387\t        val reds        = c.deltas.filter(_.verdict == Verdict.Regressed)\n388\t        val wins        = c.deltas.filter(_.verdict == Verdict.Faster)\n389\t        val unexplained = c.deltas.filter(_.unexplained)\n390\t\n391\t        val sessionWarning =\n392\t            if Bench.sameSession(control, variant) then \"\"\n393\t            else\n394\t                // comparing across sessions is what made a parity row look like a regression\n395\t                \"\\u274c These runs are from different sessions, so the deltas below are not comparable. \" +\n396\t                    \"Re-measure the control beside the variant.\\n\\n\"\n397\t\n398\t        val noiseNote =\n399\t            val n = Bench.noiseShare(variant)\n400\t            if n < 25.0 then \"\"\n401\t            else f\"\\n\\u2139\\ufe0f  $n%.0f%% of sampled time is in classes no kernel change can move, so kernel-attributable movement is a fraction of each delta above.\"\n402\t\n403\t        val bothWays =\n404\t            if wins.isEmpty || reds.isEmpty then \"\"\n405\t            else\n406\t                \"\\n\\u26a0\\ufe0f  This change both wins and loses. Those are two diagnoses, not one tradeoff: the loss usually turns out \" +\n407\t                    \"removable, and accepting it early ships a defect the same afternoon's work would have deleted.\"\n408\t\n409\t        val resolved = c.deltas.count(d => d.verdict != Verdict.BelowResolution)\n410\t\n411\t        val verdictLine =\n412\t            // every row unresolvable is not a clean result. The branch order previously fell through\n413\t            // to the green all-clear whenever no row regressed, including when no row could be read\n414\t            // at all, and the resolution note stayed silent because it counted only Flat rows.\n415\t            if resolved == 0 && c.deltas.nonEmpty then\n416\t                s\"\\n\\u26a0\\ufe0f  Nothing was resolvable: all ${c.deltas.size} rows fell below the measurement's own error. \" +\n417\t                    \"This is not a clean run, it is an unreadable one; re-measure with more forks before drawing any conclusion.\"\n418\t            else if reds.nonEmpty then\n419\t                \"\\n🔴 Regressed, so the work is unfinished until each is diagnosed or ruled on:\\n\" +\n420\t                    reds.map(d => f\"  - ${d.row} ${d.percent}%+.1f%%\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n421\t            else if !(control.wholeClass && variant.wholeClass) then\n422\t                // the claim this refuses to make is the exact false one a subset run invited before\n423\t                \"\\n⚪ No selected row regressed. This was a subset run, so it is not a statement about the suite.\"\n424\t            else \"\\n🟢 No row regressed beyond the drift band, across the whole class.\"\n425\t\n426\t        val ladder =\n427\t            if unexplained.isEmpty then \"\"\n428\t            else\n429\t                \"\\n⚠️  Moved with nothing in the evidence behind it, so the cause is not known yet:\\n\" +\n430\t                    unexplained.map(d => s\"  - ${d.row}: check allocation sites and the inlining log before proposing a mechanism\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n431\t\n432\t        val blockerBanner =\n433\t            val bs = blockers(c)\n434\t            if bs.isEmpty then \"\"\n435\t            else\n436\t                \"\\n\" + \"=\" * 78 + \"\\n\\u26d4 NOT A VALID MEASUREMENT: \" + bs.size + \" leg(s) did not reach steady state.\\n\" +\n437\t                    \"The rows below are printed in full, and none of their verdicts can be trusted: a score that\\n\" +\n438\t                    \"mixes warm and cold code is not a measurement of the code. s\"$blockerBanner$sessionWarning$header\\n$body$rampNote$resolutionNote$jit$deoptShift$polymorphic$allocSites$allocNote$partition$verdictLine$ladder$steadyState$jitTable$bothWays$noiseNote$investigation\"\n448\t Model.*\nimport kyo.*\n\n/** Persists runs so a comparison never re-runs a benchmark.\n  *\n  * Storing the whole ladder rather than a summary is what makes a later question answerable: what the JIT decided about a method, or which\n  * classes an allocation profile attributed bytes to, stays available months after the run without repeating it.\n  */\nobject Store:\n\n    def dir(root: Path): Path = root / \"runs\"\n\n    def save(root: Path, run: Run)(using Frame): Path < (Sync & Abort[FileWriteException]) =\n        val file = dir(root) / s\"${run.id}.json\"\n        file.write(Json.encode(run)).andThen(file)\n\n    def load(root: Path, id: String)(using Frame): Run < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException | FileReadException | Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n        val file = dir(root) / s\"$id.json\"\n        file.exists.map {\n            case true =>\n                file.read.map { raw =>\n                    Json.decode[Run](raw) match\n                        case Result.Success(r) => r\n                        case other             => Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"run $id is unreadable: $other\"))\n                }\n            // the raw FileNotFoundException names a path the operator never typed and says nothing\n            // about what they could have typed instead. `bench list` is one command away, so the\n            // failure runs it for them.\n            case false =>\n                ids(root).map { known =>\n                    Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(\n                        s\"no run '$id' in store $root\" +\n                            (if known.isEmpty then \", which holds no runs\"\n                             else s\". It holds ${known.size}:\\n\" + known.map(k => s\"  $k\").mkString(\"\\n\"))\n                    ))\n                }\n        }\n    end load\n\n    /** The run ids a store holds, without decoding any of them. */\n    def ids(root: Path)(using Frame): Chunk[String] < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException | Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n        requireStore(root).andThen(\n            dir(root).list.map(_.flatMap(f => Chunk.from(f.name.filter(_.endsWith(\".json\")).map(_.dropRight(5)))).sorted)\n        )\n\n    /** Fails when the store is not there at all.\n      *\n      * A missing store used to read as an empty one: `bench list --store <typo>` printed \"no runs\n      * stored\" and exited 0, so a mistyped path was indistinguishable from a store whose runs really\n      * were gone. That is the shape of failure this whole harness exists to refuse, arriving through\n      * its own front door.\n      */\n    def requireStore(root: Path)(using Frame): Unit < (Sync & Abort[Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n        dir(root).exists.map { ok =>\n            Abort.when(!ok)(Bench.BracketFailed(\n                s\"no store at $root (there is no ${dir(root).name.getOrElse(\"runs\")}/ directory under it). \" +\n                    \"A store is created by `run` or `bracket`; if you expected runs here, the path is wrong.\"\n            ))\n        }\n\n    def list(root: Path)(using Frame): Chunk[Run] < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException | FileReadException | Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n        requireStore(root).andThen {\n            dir(root).list.map { files =>\n                Kyo.foreach(files.filter(_.name.exists(_.endsWith(\".json\")))) { f =>\n                    f.read.map { raw =>\n                        Json.decode[Run](raw) match\n                            case Result.Success(r) => r\n                            case other             => Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"${f.name} is unreadable: $other\"))\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n    /** Recovers a session from any run that recorded it, so later legs join the same one. */\n    def session(root: Path, id: String)(using Frame): Session < (Sync & Abort[FileFsException | FileReadException | Bench.BracketFailed]) =\n        list(root).map { runs =>\n            runs.find(_.session.id == id) match\n                case Some(r) => r.session\n                case None    => Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"no stored run belongs to session $id\"))\n        }\n\nend Store\n\n/** Renders a comparison.\n  *\n  * The rules the skill states are enforced here rather than remembered: a verdict about the whole class is unreachable from a subset run, a\n  * movement with nothing in the evidence behind it is labelled unexplained rather than narrated, and a run that skipped the ladder cannot\n  * present itself as attributed.\n  */\nobject Report:\n\n    /** Conditions under which the numbers below are not readable, whatever they say.\n      *\n      * Both members are the same failure: a score that mixes warm and cold code. They were previously\n      * a warning line each, one in the middle of the report and one near the end, which is a placement\n      * that assumes the reader is disciplined. The operator this tool exists for is demonstrably not,\n      * and glanced past exactly such a line on a leg whose first iteration was an outlier.\n      *\n      * So they become blockers: rendered first, under a banner, and the process exits non-zero. The\n      * data is still printed in full, because suppressing it would trade one silent failure for\n      * another; what changes is that the run cannot be mistaken for a clean one.\n      */\n    def blockers(c: Comparison): Chunk[String] =\n        val unsettled =\n            c.deltas.flatMap { d =>\n                Chunk.from(Seq(\n                    Option.when(d.control.unsettledStart)(s\"${d.row} (control) never settled: iterations ${d.control.iterations.map(x => f\"$x%.1f\").mkString(\", \")}\"),\n                    Option.when(d.variant.unsettledStart)(s\"${d.row} (variant) never settled: iterations ${d.variant.iterations.map(x => f\"$x%.1f\").mkString(\", \")}\")\n                ).flatten)\n            }\n        val compiling =\n            Chunk.from(\n                (Bench.stillCompiling(c.control).map((r, p) => f\"$r%s (control) spent ${p}%.1f%% of its measured window compiling\") ++\n                    Bench.stillCompiling(c.variant).map((r, p) => f\"$r%s (variant) spent ${p}%.1f%% of its measured window compiling\"))\n            )\n        unsettled ++ compiling\n    end blockers\n\n    /** What the A/A null establishes, and what it refuses.\n      *\n      * The null compares control legs against each other, so every row it classifies is a false\n      * positive by construction. That makes a dirty null the strongest possible statement that the\n      * session below is unreadable, and it was reported as a line of text that let the process exit 0.\n      * The unsettled-leg finding is the same shape and was already fixed this way: a reader who skims\n      * a thirty-line report skims a warning inside it, so this is a blocker with an exit code.\n      *\n      * A session with too few control legs to run a null at all is also a blocker, and for a stronger\n      * reason: it is not that the check failed, it is that the session cannot check itself.\n      */\n    def nullBlockers(null_ : Maybe[Comparison], controlLegs: Int): Chunk[String] =\n        null_ match\n            case Maybe.Present(n) =>\n                val named = n.deltas.filter(_.verdict != Verdict.Flat)\n                if named.isEmpty then Chunk.empty\n                else\n                    Chunk(\n                        s\"the A/A null classified ${named.size} row(s) comparing control legs against each other: \" +\n                            named.map(d => f\"${d.row} ${d.percent}%+.1f%% (${d.verdict})\").mkString(\", \") +\n                            \". Those verdicts are false by construction, so nothing below is readable.\"\n                    )\n            case _ =>\n                Chunk(\n                    s\"$controlLegs control leg(s) is too few to run an A/A null, so this session cannot check itself. \" +\n                        \"Five legs gives three controls and is what the threshold below assumes.\"\n                )\n\n    def nullNote(null_ : Maybe[Comparison]): String =\n        null_ match\n            case Maybe.Present(n) if n.deltas.forall(_.verdict == Verdict.Flat) =>\n                f\"A/A null: clean, no control row classified against another control leg (${n.deltas.size} rows).\\n\"\n            case _ => \"\"\n\n    /** What a two-sha comparison is structurally unable to say.\n      *\n      * A comparison of two commits measures the difference between two trees. Any statement of the\n      * form \"this row moved *because of* change X\" additionally requires that X was isolated, and two\n      * shas do not carry that: the partition between the changes inside the diff was never declared,\n      * so the harness has nothing to attribute to.\n      *\n      * This is the failure the skill records as its worked example. Two changes shipped together, a\n      * node-layout change and a currency hoist; the bundle was faster and the win was confidently\n      * attributed first to one and then to the other, and both stories were wrong as told. What\n      * settled it was running the pieces separately, which is a chain of shas rather than a pair.\n      *\n      * A configuration comparison, the same sha under two sets of JVM args, has nothing to partition\n      * and gets no note.\n      */\n    def partitionNote(control: Run, variant: Run, chainLength: Int): String =\n        if control.sha == variant.sha then\n            // a configuration comparison varies nothing but the JVM arguments, so those ARE the\n            // change under test and the report is the only place a reader can see them. The\n            // campaign's headline was stored without them and could be re-read forever without\n            // anyone being able to say what it had measured.\n            val diff = variant.jvmArgs.diff(control.jvmArgs) ++ control.jvmArgs.diff(variant.jvmArgs)\n            if diff.isEmpty then\n                if control.jvmArgs.isEmpty && variant.jvmArgs.isEmpty then\n                    \"\\n⚠️  Same sha and no recorded JVM arguments on either leg, so nothing here says \" +\n                        \"what was varied. Either this is an A/A, or it was measured before the harness \" +\n                        \"recorded configuration and the difference is unrecoverable.\"\n                else \"\"\n            else\n                s\"\\nSame sha, so this is a configuration comparison and the difference is exactly:\\n\" +\n                    diff.map(a => s\"  $a\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n        else if chainLength > 2 then\n            s\"\\nThis is one step of a $chainLength-sha chain, so the delta above is the isolated contribution of \" +\n                \"this step and nothing else moved with it.\"\n        else\n            \"\\n⚠️  Two shas, so no source-level mechanism is attributable from this comparison. The diff \" +\n                \"between them may contain any number of changes and the partition between them was never declared, \" +\n                \"so a sentence of the form 'this moved because of change X' is not supported by anything here, \" +\n                \"however plausible X is. Declare a chain of shas to isolate one.\"\n\n    /** A score rendered so its own digits survive.\n      *\n      * Two fixed decimals was the previous format and it hid the numbers behind a verdict. The row\n      * `evalFixedOverhead` measures a few nanoseconds, so a real and cleanly separated regression\n      * printed as `0.01 ± 0.00` against `0.01 ± 0.00` beside a `+26.2%`, with the error column reading\n      * as though there were no error at all. The actual values were 0.005853 and 0.007364, which any\n      * reader could have judged on sight.\n      *\n      * The skill requires that a reader can judge a result without asking what was measured or how\n      * confident it is, and requires the error column specifically because a delta smaller than the\n      * combined error is not a result. A format that rounds both to zero defeats both rules at once.\n      */\n    def score(x: Double): String =\n        val a = Math.abs(x)\n        if a == 0.0 then \"0\"\n        else if a >= 100 then f\"$x%.1f\"\n        else if a >= 1 then f\"$x%.2f\"\n        else if a >= 0.01 then f\"$x%.4f\"\n        else f\"$x%.6f\"\n\n    def icon(v: Verdict): String =\n        v match\n            case Verdict.Faster          => \"🟢\"\n            case Verdict.Flat            => \"⚪\"\n            case Verdict.Regressed       => \"🔴\"\n            case Verdict.BelowResolution => \"🔵\"\n\n    def render(c: Comparison, chainLength: Int = 2): String =\n        val control = c.control\n        val variant = c.variant\n        val scope =\n            if control.wholeClass && variant.wholeClass then s\"all ${control.declaredRows} rows\"\n            else s\"${c.deltas.size} selected rows of ${control.declaredRows}, so this says nothing about the rest\"\n        val evidence =\n            if control.evidence == Evidence.Full && variant.evidence == Evidence.Full then \"full ladder\"\n            else \"timing only, so no movement here is attributed\"\n        val forksNote = if variant.forks < 3 then s\", -f ${variant.forks} is diagnostic and not a claim\" else \"\"\n        val drift     = Bench.band(control, variant)\n        val bandNote =\n            if control.session.driftPercent > 0 then f\"drift $drift%.1f%% measured this session\"\n            else f\"drift $drift%.1f%% assumed, not measured\"\n\n        val header =\n            s\"\"\"|Control `${control.sha.take(10)}` (${control.label}) against variant `${variant.sha.take(10)}` (${variant.label}).\n                |JMH -f ${variant.forks}$forksNote, $scope, $evidence, $bandNote.\n                |Markers control ${control.markers.map(m => s\"${m.name}=${m.count}\").mkString(\" \")} | variant ${variant.markers.map(m => s\"${m.name}=${m.count}\").mkString(\" \")}\n                |\n                || | row | mode | cnt | control | variant | delta | resolves | B/op delta | mechanism |\n                ||---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\"\"\".stripMargin\n\n        // a leg whose first measured iteration sits far from the rest was still warming up, and its\n        // score and error both absorb that without showing it. Only the per-iteration series reveals\n        // it, and for an ingested run it is the only steady-state signal that exists at all.\n        val RampLimit = 0.05\n        val ramped =\n            c.deltas.flatMap { d =>\n                Chunk.from(Seq(\n                    d.control.warmupRamp.filter(_ > RampLimit).map(r => (d.row, \"control\", r)),\n                    d.variant.warmupRamp.filter(_ > RampLimit).map(r => (d.row, \"variant\", r))\n                ).flatMap(_.toOption))\n            }\n        val rampNote =\n            if ramped.isEmpty then \"\"\n            else\n                \"\\n\\u26a0\\ufe0f  A leg's first measured iteration sits far from the rest, so it was still warming up and \" +\n                    \"its score includes that ramp:\\n\" +\n                    ramped.map((row, side, r) => f\"  - $row%s ($side%s) first iteration is ${r * 100}%.0f%% from the median of the rest\")\n                        .mkString(\"\\n\")\n\n        val resolutionNote =\n            val unbounded = c.deltas.count(d => d.flatButUnbounded || d.verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution)\n            val bounded   = c.deltas.flatMap(_.resolution)\n            if bounded.nonEmpty then\n                val worst = bounded.map(_.percent).max\n                // df 0 marks a single-pair comparison: the bound is the legs' own reported error, not\n                // a threshold estimated from replicates, and the two are not the same claim\n                if bounded.head.df == 0 then\n                    f\"\\nEvery flat row below is flat to within +-${worst}%.2f%%, the floor set by the legs' own reported \" +\n                        \"error. These legs were not replicated, so this bounds the result without estimating the spread; \" +\n                        \"a replicated bracket would give a real threshold and this does not.\"\n                else\n                    f\"\\nEvery flat row below is flat to within its own resolution, at worst +-${worst}%.2f%% \" +\n                        f\"(alpha ${bounded.head.alpha}%.5f after correcting for ${c.deltas.size} rows, df ${bounded.head.df}).\"\n            else if unbounded > 0 then\n                s\"\\n⚠️  $unbounded flat rows carry no resolution: these legs were not replicated, so \" +\n                    \"'flat' here means the harness cannot say how small an effect it would have missed, not that nothing changed.\"\n            else \"\"\n\n        val body = c.deltas.map { d =>\n            val delta = if d.verdict == Verdict.BelowResolution then \"below resolution\" else f\"${d.percent}%+.1f%%\"\n            // this row's OWN threshold, not the worst across the table. The footer reports only the\n            // worst, which cannot answer the question a flat row actually raises: was it close to\n            // resolving, or nowhere near? On the replicated sweep two rows at -12.5% and -10.7% came\n            // back flat while a -7.1% row was a win, and the table gave no way to see why.\n            val res = d.resolution.map(r => f\"±${r.percent}%.1f%%\").getOrElse(\"-\")\n            val alloc = d.allocDelta.map(a => f\"$a%+.0f\").getOrElse(\"-\")\n            val mech =\n                if d.mechanism.nonEmpty then d.mechanism.mkString(\"; \")\n                else if d.unexplained then \"**none found**\"\n                else \"-\"\n            f\"| ${icon(d.verdict)} | `${d.row}` | ${d.control.mode} | ${d.variant.count} | \" +\n                s\"${score(d.control.score)} ± ${score(d.control.error)} | ${score(d.variant.score)} ± ${score(d.variant.error)} | $delta | $res | $alloc | $mech |\"\n        }.mkString(\"\\n\")\n\n        val jit =\n            if c.jitChanges.isEmpty then \"\"\n            else \"\\nInlining changed:\\n\" + c.jitChanges.map(s => s\"  - $s\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n\n        val deoptShift =\n            val cd = control.deopts.map(d => d.reason -> d.count).toMap\n            val moved = variant.deopts.filter(d => Math.abs(d.count - cd.getOrElse(d.reason, 0)) > cd.getOrElse(d.reason, 0) / 4 + 5)\n            if moved.isEmpty then \"\"\n            else\n                \"\\nDeoptimization changed, which no timing or allocation figure explains:\\n\" +\n                    moved.map(d => s\"  - ${d.reason}: ${cd.getOrElse(d.reason, 0)} -> ${d.count}\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n\n        val steadyState =\n            val cs = Bench.stillCompiling(control)\n            val vs = Bench.stillCompiling(variant)\n            if cs.isEmpty && vs.isEmpty then \"\"\n            else\n                \"\\n\\U0001f6d1 NOT STEADY STATE. These rows were still being compiled while they were measured, so the scores mix compiled \" +\n                    \"and compiling code. Do not read the deltas above until this is diagnosed. Warming longer would hide it: a benchmark \" +\n                    \"that needs unusual warmup is reporting something about the code under it.\\n\" +\n                    (cs.map((r, p) => f\"  - control $r%s spent ${p}%.1f%% of its window compiling\") ++\n                        vs.map((r, p) => f\"  - variant $r%s spent ${p}%.1f%% of its window compiling\")).mkString(\"\\n\") +\n                    \"\\n  Start from the JIT metrics below: more tasks, more recompilation or more deopts on one leg is the cause, not noise.\"\n\n        val jitTable =\n            (control.jit_metrics, variant.jit_metrics) match\n                case (Maybe.Present(c), Maybe.Present(v)) =>\n                    def row(n: String, a: Double, b: Double, unit: String = \"\") =\n                        val d = if a == 0.0 then \"\" else f\" (${(b - a) / a * 100}%+.0f%%)\"\n                        f\"| $n%-24s | $a%10.0f$unit | $b%10.0f$unit |$d |\"\n                    \"\\n\\nJIT cost, which is a property of the design and not only of the run:\\n\" +\n                        \"| metric | control | variant | |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n\" +\n                        Seq(\n                            row(\"compiling in window\", c.msInWindow, v.msInWindow, \"ms\"),\n                            row(\"compiling total\", c.msTotal, v.msTotal, \"ms\"),\n                            row(\"compilation tasks\", c.tasks.toDouble, v.tasks.toDouble),\n                            row(\"C2 tasks\", c.c2Tasks.toDouble, v.c2Tasks.toDouble),\n                            row(\"OSR tasks\", c.osrTasks.toDouble, v.osrTasks.toDouble),\n                            row(\"methods recompiled\", c.recompiled.toDouble, v.recompiled.toDouble),\n                            // runtime events only. The planted-guard census used to sit in this row\n                            // and swamped it: 633 guards against 6 real deoptimizations.\n                            row(\"runtime deopts\", c.runtimeDeopts.toDouble, v.runtimeDeopts.toDouble),\n                            row(\"made not entrant\", c.madeNotEntrant.toDouble, v.madeNotEntrant.toDouble),\n                            row(\"last compile at\", c.lastCompileAt, v.lastCompileAt, \"s\")\n                        ).mkString(\"\\n\")\n                case _ => \"\"\n\n        val polymorphic =\n            // only sites the JIT actually profiled a receiver for. The previous version filtered on\n            // `!monomorphic`, which included every unprofiled site, and printed 46 of 47 of them\n            // under a heading promising measured receiver counts while each had a receiver count of\n            // zero. Absence of a profile is not evidence of polymorphism.\n            val poly = variant.morphism.filter(_.monomorphic.contains(false)).take(3)\n            if poly.isEmpty then \"\"\n            else\n                \"\\nPolymorphic call sites, among the few the JIT profiled a receiver for:\\n\" +\n                    poly.map(m => s\"  - ${m.callee} ${m.count} calls, ${m.receiverCount} to the top receiver\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n\n        // an allocation change is exact and per-operation, so it does not need the timing to resolve.\n        // A row can be flat in time and still allocate 240,000 B/op more, and suppressing the\n        // mechanism on flat rows hid exactly that: the only visible trace was a number in a column.\n        val allocMoved =\n            c.deltas.filter(d => d.verdict != Verdict.Regressed && d.allocDelta.exists(a => Math.abs(a) > 1.0))\n        val allocNote =\n            if allocMoved.isEmpty then \"\"\n            else\n                \"\\n\\u2139\\ufe0f  Allocation moved on rows whose timing did not resolve. Allocation is exact and per-operation, \" +\n                    \"so this is a real change regardless of what the timing could or could not show:\\n\" +\n                    allocMoved.map(d => f\"  - ${d.row}%s ${d.allocDelta.getOrElse(0.0)}%+.0f B/op, timing ${d.percent}%+.1f%% (${d.verdict})\").mkString(\"\\n\")\n\n        // which method minted the class whose bytes moved. 1.0) / (a + b + 2.0) then front * betaContinuedFraction(a, b, x) / a\n            else 1.0 - front * betaContinuedFraction(b, a, 1.0 - x) / b\n\n    /** Two-sided tail probability of Student's t: P(|T| > t) for the given degrees of freedom. */\n    def tTailTwoSided(df: Int, t: Double): Double =\n        if df <= 0 then 1.0\n        else incompleteBeta(df / 2.0, 0.5, df / (df + t * t))\n\n    /** Two-sided Student t critical value, computed rather than tabulated.\n      *\n      * A table was tried first and was wrong in two ways that a table is always liable to be: it returned infinity for any degrees of freedom\n      * it happened to omit (7 and 9, both reachable from ordinary leg counts), which silently classified a 100% regression as *flat* and\n      * printed \"detectable at +-Infinity%\" under a green all-clear; and its fallback for an untabulated alpha was *looser* than the truth\n      * while its comment claimed the opposite, so tightening the Bonferroni correction from 15 rows to 16 would have loosened the test.\n      *\n      * Bisection on the exact tail probability has neither failure mode and is about as much code as the table was.\n      */\n    def tCritical(df: Int, alpha: Double): Double =\n        if df <= 0 then Double.PositiveInfinity\n        else if alpha <= 0.0 then Double.PositiveInfinity\n        else if alpha >= 1.0 then 0.0\n        else\n            var lo = 0.0\n            var hi = 1.0\n            // expand until the tail at `hi` is below alpha, so the root is bracketed\n            while tTailTwoSided(df, hi) > alpha && hi < 1e12 do hi *= 2.0\n            var i = 0\n            while i < 200 do\n                val mid = (lo + hi) / 2.0\n                if tTailTwoSided(df, mid) > alpha then lo = mid else hi = mid\n                i += 1\n            (lo + hi) / 2.0\n\n    /** One row measured across the replicate legs of one session. */\n    case class Replicated(row: String, control: Chunk[Double], variant: Chunk[Double], legError: Chunk[Double] = Chunk.empty) derives Schema:\n        /** The largest relative error any single leg reported for itself, as a fraction.\n          *\n          * A threshold derived only from between-leg spread can come out tighter than the uncertainty\n          * of the legs it is built from, and then it classifies that uncertainty as a result. A real\n          * A/A bracket did exactly this: five legs of identical sources, each leg reporting +-5.2% of\n          * its own, produced a 2.60% threshold and called a 3.8% difference a regression. The retired\n          * drift estimator had this floor (`max(spread, ownError)`) and the replicate statistic lost\n          * it.\n          */\n        def ownError: Double = if legError.isEmpty then 0.0 else legError.max\n\n        def nC: Int             = control.size\n        def nV: Int             = variant.size\n        def controlMean: Double = if nC == 0 then 0.0 else control.sum / nC\n        def variantMean: Double = if nV == 0 then 0.0 else variant.sum / nV\n\n        /** Pooled within-group standard deviation, the only honest estimate of run-to-run spread available.\n          *\n          * A single absolute difference between two control legs is a draw from a distribution, not a threshold; using it as one is what made\n          * the previous design classify noise half the time.\n          */\n        def pooledSd: Maybe[Double] =\n            val df = degreesOfFreedom\n            if df <= 0 then Maybe.empty\n            else\n                val ssC = control.map(x => (x - controlMean) * (x - controlMean)).sum\n                val ssV = variant.map(x => (x - variantMean) * (x - variantMean)).sum\n                Maybe(Math.sqrt((ssC + ssV) / df))\n\n        def degreesOfFreedom: Int = Math.max(0, (nC - 1) + (nV - 1))\n\n        /** Standard error of the difference of means. */\n        def standardError: Maybe[Double] =\n            if nC == 0 || nV == 0 then Maybe.empty\n            else pooledSd.map(sd => sd * Math.sqrt(1.0 / nC + 1.0 / nV))\n\n        def deltaPercent: Double = if controlMean == 0.0 then 0.0 else (variantMean - controlMean) / controlMean * 100\n    end Replicated\n\n    /** Per-row alpha after correcting for testing every row of the class at once.\n      *\n      * Fifteen independent tests at 5% each produce at least one false positive 54% of the time. Bonferroni is the conservative choice and\n      * the one that can be stated in a sentence, which matters more here than the power a sharper correction would buy.\n      */\n    def perRowAlpha(familyAlpha: Double, rows: Int): Double =\n        if rows <= 0 then familyAlpha else familyAlpha / rows\n\n    def threshold(r: Replicated, familyAlpha: Double, rows: Int): Maybe[Resolution] =\n        val alpha = perRowAlpha(familyAlpha, rows)\n        r.standardError.map { se =>\n            val t = tCritical(r.degreesOfFreedom, alpha)\n            // never tighter than the legs' own reported uncertainty: a threshold below that\n            // classifies the measurement's own error as a result\n            val abs = Math.max(t * se, r.ownError * r.controlMean)\n            Resolution(if r.controlMean == 0.0 then 0.0 else abs / r.controlMean * 100, abs, r.degreesOfFreedom, alpha)\n        }\n\n    /** Classifies one row against its own threshold. A row whose spread cannot be estimated is unresolved, never flat. */\n    def classify(r: Replicated, familyAlpha: Double, rows: Int): (Verdict, Maybe[Resolution]) =\n        val th = threshold(r, familyAlpha, rows)\n        th match\n            case Maybe.Present(t) =>\n                val diff = r.variantMean - r.controlMean\n                if Math.abs(diff) <= t.absolute then (Verdict.Flat, th)\n                else if diff < 0 then (Verdict.Faster, th)\n                else (Verdict.Regressed, th)\n            case _ => (Verdict.BelowResolution, th)\n    end classify\n\n    /** Common-mode drift across the session, estimated as the median per-row control trend.\n      *\n      * Reported rather than spent: if every row moves the same way by the same amount, that is the machine warming, and the replicate design\n      * already cancels it from the estimator. Charging it to the band as well would inflate every threshold by a quantity that has already\n      * been removed, which is the contradiction the previous design carried.\n      */\n    def commonMode(rs: Chunk[Replicated]): Maybe[Double] =\n        val trends =\n            rs.flatMap { r =>\n                if r.control.size < 2 then Chunk.empty\n                else Chunk((r.control.last - r.control.head) / (if r.controlMean == 0.0 then 1.0 else r.controlMean) * 100)\n            }\n        median(trends)\n\n    /** Per-row residual after removing the session's common mode: the part that is this row's own noise. */\n    def residual(r: Replicated, common: Double): Maybe[Double] =\n        if r.control.size < 2 then Maybe.empty\n        else\n            val trend = (r.control.last - r.control.head) / (if r.controlMean == 0.0 then 1.0 else r.controlMean) * 100\n            Maybe(Math.abs(trend - common))\n\n    def median(xs: Chunk[Double]): Maybe[Double] =\n        if xs.isEmpty then Maybe.empty\n        else\n            val s = xs.sorted\n            val n = s.size\n            Maybe(if n % 2 == 1 then s(n / 2) else (s(n / 2 - 1) + s(n / 2)) / 2.0)\n\nend Stats\n","numLines":205,"startLine":1,"totalLines":205}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"ed1a444b-6bc9-4db1-b975-4bf54363dbed","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}

That was discovered by running the session and reading the footer, which\n  * is the expensive order. Worse, `trailingMapsStayLinear` resolves to ±22.64%, so three separate\n  * runs were spent reporting a 25% timing regression on a row that cannot support a verdict of that\n  * size, and each was believed at the time.\n  *\n  * Everything needed to say so first is already stored: any prior run on the same rows carries each\n  * leg's own error, and a bracket's resolution follows from that plus the leg count.\n  *\n  * Calibration says forks do not help. Tripling them cut each leg's own error six-fold and moved the\n  * resolution by 0.05 points, because the variance is between legs rather than within them. So the\n  * answer this gives is in legs, and it says that rather than leaving the reader to discover it.\n  */\nobject Plan:\n\n    /** What one row could resolve at a given leg count.\n      *\n      * `fromReplicates` records which quantity the estimate rests on, because they are not the same\n      * and confusing them is how this file was wrong on its first run. A single leg reports the\n      * spread of its own iterations; a bracket's threshold rests on the spread *between* legs. For\n      * `continuationBodiesFuse` those are ±1.9% and ±0.9%, so a forecast from one leg called the row\n      * unresolvable at ±14.6% while a real bracket resolved a -6.8% win on it.\n      */\n    case class Forecast(\n        row: String,\n        priorError: Double,\n        legs: Int,\n        resolvable: Double,\n        fromReplicates: Boolean,\n        /** True when the spread came from one arm only, which biases the forecast optimistic. */\n        oneArm: Boolean = false\n    ) derives Schema:\n        def canSee(target: Double): Boolean = target >= resolvable\n\n        def show: String =\n            val basis =\n                if !fromReplicates then \"within-leg, an approximation\"\n                else if oneArm then \"one arm only, optimistic\"\n                else \"both arms, pooled\"\n            f\"$row%-34s $basis%-28s ±${priorError * 100}%.1f%%  ->  resolves ±${resolvable * 100}%.1f%% at $legs legs\"\n\n    /** Estimate the detectable effect for each row of a stored run.\n      *\n      * The estimate is the leg's own relative error scaled by the standard error of a difference of\n      * means over the planned split, times the t critical value the real comparison would use. It is\n      * an estimate and is labelled one: the true spread is between legs and a prior single run can\n      * only approximate it.\n      */\n    def forecast(priors: Chunk[Run], legs: Int, familyAlpha: Double): Chunk[Forecast] =\n        val nC   = (legs + 1) / 2\n        val nV   = legs / 2\n        val df   = Math.max(0, (nC - 1) + (nV - 1))\n        val rows = priors.headMaybe.map(_.rows.map(_.name)).getOrElse(Chunk.empty)\n        val t    = Stats.tCritical(df, Stats.perRowAlpha(familyAlpha, rows.size))\n        Chunk.from(\n            rows.map { name =>\n                // Split by arm and pool WITHIN each, which is what `Stats.pooledSd` does and therefore\n                // what the threshold being forecast actually rests on. Lumping every prior into one\n                // spread is wrong twice over: given one arm it sees only that arm's variance, and\n                // given both it folds the real difference between them into the \"spread\" and inflates\n                // the forecast instead.\n                //\n                // Measured against the replicated sweep, the one-arm version under-predicted:\n                // `continuationBodiesFuse` forecast +-1.9% against an actual +-3.6%, and\n                // `handleLoopAnswersInPlace` +-10.0% against +-14.4%, because the variant legs carry\n                // more spread than the controls and a control-only forecast cannot see it.\n                def armScores(arm: String) =\n                    Chunk.from(priors.filter(_.label.startsWith(arm)).flatMap(_.row(name)).map(_.score))\n                val ctl  = armScores(\"control\")\n                val vnt  = armScores(\"variant\")\n                val arms = Chunk(ctl, vnt).filter(_.size >= 2)\n                val all = Chunk.from(priors.flatMap(_.row(name)).map(_.score))\n                // normalised against the CONTROL mean when there is one, because that is what\n                // `Stats.threshold` divides by. Using the mean of every leg understates the forecast\n                // whenever the arms genuinely differ: on `trailingMapsStayLinear`, whose variant runs\n                // a third slower than its control, that alone put the forecast 8.8 points below the\n                // threshold it was predicting.\n                val mean =\n                    if ctl.nonEmpty then ctl.sum / ctl.size\n                    else if all.isEmpty then 0.0\n                    else all.sum / all.size\n\n                def pooled(groups: Chunk[Chunk[Double]]): Maybe[Double] =\n                    val df = groups.map(_.size - 1).sum\n                    if df <= 0 then Maybe.empty\n                    else\n                        val ss = groups.map { g =>\n                            val m = g.sum / g.size\n                            g.map(x => (x - m) * (x - m)).sum\n                        }.sum\n                        Maybe(Math.sqrt(ss / df))\n\n                val (rel, replicated) =\n                    pooled(arms) match\n                        case Maybe.Present(sd) if mean > 0.0 && arms.size >= 2 => (sd / mean, true)\n                        case Maybe.Present(sd) if mean > 0.0                   => (sd / mean, true)\n                        case _ =>\n                            if all.size >= 2 && mean > 0.0 then\n                                val sd = Math.sqrt(all.map(x => (x - mean) * (x - mean)).sum / (all.size - 1))\n                                (sd / mean, true)\n                            else\n                                (priors.headMaybe.flatMap(_.row(name)).map(_.relativeError).getOrElse(0.0), false)\n                val oneArm = arms.size < 2\n                val se     = rel * Math.sqrt(1.0 / nC + 1.0 / nV)\n                // the same floor `Stats.threshold` applies: a threshold below the legs' own reported\n                // uncertainty would classify that uncertainty as a result. Forecasting without it\n                // predicts a resolution the real comparison will never award.\n                val ownError = priors.flatMap(_.row(name)).map(_.relativeError).maxOption.getOrElse(0.0)\n                Forecast(name, rel, legs, Math.max(t * se, ownError), replicated, oneArm)\n            }.sortBy(-_.resolvable)\n        )\n\n    /** Rows that cannot support a verdict about an effect of the given size. */\n    def blind(fs: Chunk[Forecast], target: Double): Chunk[Forecast] = Chunk.from(fs.filterNot(_.canSee(target)))\n\nend Plan\n","numLines":122,"startLine":1,"totalLines":122}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"20095e0d-03ea-4e30-9c22-f98e9598896f","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}
