Two candidate falsifiers from earlier drafts\n      * are deliberately absent: megamorphism, because the log profiles a receiver at 12 sites out of\n      * 5,093 and the hypothesis is not statable from that; and GC ergonomics, because every leg pins\n      * the heap and the collector, so the condition cannot arise without unpinning them.\n      */\n    def falsifiers(c: Comparison): Chunk[Falsifier] =\n        val regressed = c.deltas.filter(_.verdict == Verdict.Regressed)\n        val wins      = c.deltas.filter(_.verdict == Verdict.Faster)\n\n        // a method the control inlined everywhere and the variant refuses everywhere is the\n        // strongest form of this hypothesis, and the only one a single flag can address\n        val stopped =\n            val before = c.control.jit.map(v => v.method -> v).toMap\n            c.variant.jit.filter { v =>\n                v.alwaysRefused && before.get(v.method).exists(_.alwaysInlined)\n            }\n        val stoppedFalsifiers =\n            if regressed.isEmpty then Chunk.empty\n            else\n                stopped.map { v =>\n                    Falsifier(\n                        Hypothesis.StoppedInlining(v.method),\n                        Arm.Variant,\n                        Seq(s\"-XX:CompileCommandFile=<file with: inline ${commandForm(v.method)}>\"),\n                        s\"if the ${regressed.size} regressed row(s) recover, the refusal is the cause; if they do not, it is not\"\n                    )\n                }\n\n        // a method sitting just over a budget is the case where raising the budget is a clean\n        // single-variable experiment. Well over it, the flag would change decisions everywhere\n        val budget =\n            c.variant.jit.flatMap { v =>\n                v.nearBudget match\n                    case Maybe.Present(_) if regressed.nonEmpty =>\n                        val (name, limit) = if v.bytes <= 70 then (\"MaxInlineSize\", 35) else (\"FreqInlineSize\", 325)\n                        Chunk(Falsifier(\n                            Hypothesis.ExceededBudget(v.method, name, limit),\n                            Arm.Variant,\n                            Seq(s\"-XX:$name=${v.bytes + 1}\"),\n                            s\"raising only the budget this method is over separates 'too big for the budget' from 'the wrong shape'\"\n                        ))\n                    case _ => Chunk.empty\n            }\n\n        // the cheap direction first: contradicting the win on the control costs one run and can\n        // dissolve the case for the design change entirely\n        val winFalsifiers =\n            if wins.isEmpty then Chunk.empty\n            else\n                val after = c.variant.jit.map(v => v.method -> v).toMap\n                c.control.jit.filter(v => v.alwaysRefused && after.get(v.method).exists(_.alwaysInlined)).map { v =>\n                    Falsifier(\n                        Hypothesis.WinFromInlining(v.method),\n                        Arm.Control,\n                        Seq(s\"-XX:CompileCommandFile=<file with: inline ${commandForm(v.method)}>\"),\n                        \"if the control reaches the variant's number, the win is the inlining and not the design\"\n                    )\n                }\n\n        // an allocation change with no timing change, or a large one either way, is the signature\n        // this asks about: an enlarged compilation unit defeating escape analysis\n        val scalar =\n            c.deltas.filter(_.allocDelta.exists(a => Math.abs(a) > 1000.0)).map { d =>\n                Falsifier(\n                    Hypothesis.RidesScalarReplacement(d.row),\n                    Arm.Control,\n                    Seq(\"-XX:-EliminateAllocations\"),\n                    f\"if disabling escape analysis on the control reproduces the variant's ${d.allocDelta.getOrElse(0.0)}%+.0f B/op, \" +\n                        \"the variant destroyed a scalar replacement rather than adding an allocation\"\n                )\n            }\n\n        stoppedFalsifiers ++ budget ++ winFalsifiers ++ scalar\n    end falsifiers\n\n    /** `pkg.Class::method` is how the log names a site; `pkg.Class::method` is also what\n      * CompileCommand wants, but with the class in its own field. Kept as one function so the two\n      * spellings cannot drift apart silently.\n      */\n    def commandForm(logMethod: String): String =\n        logMethod.split(\"::\") match\n            case Array(cls, m) => s\"$cls::$m\"\n            case _             => logMethod\n\n    /** Whether the instructed flag actually changed what it was supposed to change, and nothing else.\n      *\n      * Returns the reason it did not, or empty when it did. Both halves matter: a flag that took at\n      * no site establishes nothing, and a flag that moved five other methods' verdicts as well has\n      * run a different experiment from the one that was asked for.\n      */\n    def efficacy(h: Hypothesis, before: Run, after: Run): Maybe[String] =\n        h.target match\n            case Maybe.Absent => Maybe.empty\n            case Maybe.Present(m) =>\n                val was = before.jit.find(_.method == m)\n                val now = after.jit.find(_.method == m)\n                (was, now) match\n                    case (None, _) => Maybe(s\"$m has no verdict in the baseline leg, so nothing can be said to have moved\")\n                    case (_, None) => Maybe(s\"$m has no verdict in the isolation leg; the method was not compiled there at all\")\n                    case (Some(b), Some(a)) =>\n                        if b.inlined == a.inlined && b.refused == a.refused then\n                            Maybe(\n                                s\"the flag did not take: $m is still ${b.inlined} inlined / ${b.refused} refused. \" +\n                                    \"HotSpot treats an inline command as a hint and still refuses on MaxInlineLevel, node budget, \" +\n                                    \"or a method it cannot compile.\"\n                            )\n                        else\n                            val others =\n                                val map = before.jit.map(v => v.method -> v).toMap\n                                after.jit.filter(v => v.method != m && map.get(v.method).exists(b2 => b2.inlined != v.inlined || b2.refused != v.refused))\n                            if others.isEmpty then Maybe.empty\n                            else\n                                Maybe(\n                                    s\"${others.size} other method(s) changed verdict too (${others.take(3).map(_.method).mkString(\", \")}), \" +\n                                        \"so this run changed more than one thing and attributes nothing. Forcing a callee spends the \" +\n                                        \"caller's remaining budget, which is how that happens.\"\n                                )\n    end efficacy\n\n    /** Which measured quantity answers a hypothesis.\n      *\n      * Not a detail: `RidesScalarReplacement` is a claim about bytes per operation, and adjudicating\n      * it against wall clock reads the wrong column and answers a question nobody asked. That is what\n      * this did on its first outing against real data, where the row it fires on is one whose timing\n      * does not resolve at all and whose allocation is exact.\n      */\n    enum Quantity derives CanEqual:\n        case Time, Allocation\n\n        def of(r: Row): Maybe[Double] =\n            this match\n                case Time       => Maybe(r.score)\n                case Allocation => r.allocPerOp\n\n        /** Allocation is nearly exact, and \"nearly\" is measured rather than assumed.\n          *\n          * Across four A/A sets of three legs each on identical sources, every row that allocates\n          * kilobytes reproduced its `gc.alloc.rate.norm` to the byte. The one row that allocates\n          * megabytes did not: `trailingMapsStayLinear` spread 47.8 B on 2.32 MB in one set and 24.2 B\n          * in another, so 2.1e-5 relative at worst.\n          *\n          * A flat one-byte threshold was tried first and it refused the campaign's own escape-analysis\n          * result: the isolation landed 23.8 B from its target on 2.56 MB, which is a reproduction to\n          * six significant figures, and was reported inconclusive. The band is therefore relative,\n          * at 5e-5, a little over twice the worst spread ever observed here, with a one-byte floor so\n          * the rows that really are exact stay exact. On the 240,000 B/op effect this has to resolve,\n          * that band is 128 bytes, so it costs nothing that matters.\n          */\n        def resolution(b: Row, i: Row): Double =\n            this match\n                case Time => Math.max(b.relativeError, i.relativeError) * Math.max(b.score, i.score)\n                case Allocation =>\n                    val scale = Math.max(b.allocPerOp.getOrElse(0.0), i.allocPerOp.getOrElse(0.0))\n                    Math.max(1.0, 5e-5 * scale)\n\n        def unit: String = if this == Time then \"\" else \" B/op\"\n    end Quantity\n\n    def quantity(h: Hypothesis): Quantity =\n        h match\n            case Hypothesis.RidesScalarReplacement(_) => Quantity.Allocation\n            case _                                    => Quantity.Time\n\n    /** Adjudicates one falsifier from the run it produced.\n      *\n      * `baseline` is the leg the hypothesis is about, `isolation` the same leg re-run under the flag,\n      * and `target` the number the hypothesis predicts the isolation will reach, in whichever quantity\n      * the hypothesis is about. The recovery threshold is the legs' own resolution rather than a fixed\n      * percentage, because a leg that cannot resolve the effect cannot answer the question either way,\n      * and saying so is a result.\n      */\n    def adjudicate(\n        f: Falsifier,\n        row: String,\n        baseline: Run,\n        isolation: Run,\n        target: Double\n    ): Outcome =\n        val q = quantity(f.hypothesis)\n        efficacy(f.hypothesis, baseline, isolation) match\n            case Maybe.Present(why) => Outcome.Inconclusive(why)\n            case Maybe.Absent =>\n                (baseline.rows.find(_.name == row), isolation.rows.find(_.name == row)) match\n                    case (Some(bb), Some(ii)) =>\n                        (q.of(bb), q.of(ii)) match\n                            case (Maybe.Present(b), Maybe.Present(i)) =>\n                                val resolution = q.resolution(bb, ii)\n                                val gap        = Math.abs(b - target)\n                                if gap <= resolution then\n                                    Outcome.Inconclusive(\n                                        f\"the baseline is already within its own resolution of the target (${gap}%.2f against +-${resolution}%.2f${q.unit}), \" +\n                                            \"so this experiment could not have separated them whatever it returned\"\n                                    )\n                                else if Math.abs(i - target) <= resolution then\n                                    Outcome.Confirmed(f\"$row moved from ${b}%.2f to ${i}%.2f${q.unit}, reaching ${target}%.2f within +-${resolution}%.2f\")\n                                else if Math.abs(i - b) <= resolution then\n                                    Outcome.Refuted(f\"$row stayed at ${i}%.2f${q.unit} against ${b}%.2f while the flag demonstrably took; the delta is not this\")\n                                else\n                                    Outcome.Inconclusive(\n                                        f\"$row moved from ${b}%.2f to ${i}%.2f${q.unit}, which is neither the target ${target}%.2f nor no move at all\"\n                                    )\n                            case _ =>\n                                Outcome.Inconclusive(\n                                    s\"$row carries no ${if q == Quantity.Allocation then \"allocation figure\" else \"score\"} on one of the legs, \" +\n                                        \"so the quantity this hypothesis is about was never measured\"\n                                )\n                    case _ => Outcome.Inconclusive(s\"$row is missing from one of the two legs\")\n        end match\n    end adjudicate\n\n    /** The report the investigator adds to a comparison. */\n    def render(c: Comparison): String =\n        val fs = falsifiers(c)\n        if fs.isEmpty then \"\"\n        else\n            \"\\n\\nNext experiments, each one run of a configuration this harness already issues:\\n\" +\n                fs.zipWithIndex.map((f, i) => s\"  ${i + 1}. ${f.show}\").mkString(\"\\n\") +\n                \"\\n  A falsifier whose flag did not take refutes nothing; the run reports that as inconclusive \" +\n                \"rather than as evidence against the hypothesis.\"\n\nend Investigate\n","numLines":309,"startLine":1,"totalLines":309}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"5f728066-bdf9-4020-aa7a-b6ba43548b1c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}

Here every decision sits beside the `<method>` element that\n8\t  * declares the callee's size, in structure, and the log additionally carries what that one cannot:\n9\t  *\n10\t  *   - deoptimizations that actually happened, which are invisible everywhere else\n11\t  *   - receiver counts per call site, so monomorphic against megamorphic is measured rather than asserted\n12\t  *   - OSR compilations, which is where a benchmark's loop body actually lives\n13\t  *\n14\t  * Ids are scoped to a compilation task and reused across tasks, so the symbol table is rebuilt per `<task>`.\n15\t  *\n16\t  * Three distinctions here were each responsible for a wrong conclusion, and are preserved deliberately:\n17\t  *\n18\t  *   1. A call site with no `receiver` attribute is *unprofiled*, not megamorphic.\n19\t  *   2. An `<uncommon_trap>` with `thread=` is an event; one with `bci=` is a guard the compiler planted.\n20\t  *   3. A method's inlining verdict is per site. It has a denominator, and reporting it without one is a coin flip.\n21\t  */\n22\tobject LogCompilation:\n23\t\n24\t    // `<call>` appears in two forms: the C2 form carrying `count` (and sometimes `receiver`), and the C1 form carrying only `instr`.\n25\t    // Matching just the first silently dropped 4456 of 5093 elements, so the shape is matched first and the attributes read after.\n26\t    private val Call       = \"\"\"<call [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n27\t    private val AttrMethod = \"\"\"method='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n28\t    // boundary-anchored: an unanchored `count='` also matches `receiver_count='`, which reads\n29\t    // correctly today only because count always precedes it. On a site where it did not, the parser\n30\t    // would take the receiver count as the call count and then call the site monomorphic, since\n31\t    // `recvd == count` becomes trivially true.\n32\t    private val AttrCount  = \"\"\"(?<![\\w_])count='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n33\t    private val AttrRecv   = \"\"\"receiver='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n34\t    private val AttrRecvN  = \"\"\"receiver_count='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n35\t\n36\t    // by shape, for the same reason as the rest: fixing `id` before `name` is one reordering away\n37\t    // from silently dropping the symbol table\n38\t    private val Klass = \"\"\"<klass [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n39\t    // `bytes` and `iicount` are absent on the `unloaded='1'` form, so requiring both dropped 89 of 4466 declarations and left 118 call\n40\t    // sites resolving to raw ids downstream.\n41\t    private val Method     = \"\"\"<method [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n42\t    private val AttrId     = \"\"\"(?<![\\w_])id='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n43\t    private val AttrHolder = \"\"\"holder='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n44\t    /** The log is XML, so its attribute values are escaped, and a constructor arrives as `&lt;init&gt;`.\n45\t      *\n46\t      * Every other tool in this ladder prints `<init>`: javap, async-profiler, the JVM's own\n47\t      * `PrintInlining`. A name that agrees with none of them cannot be cross-referenced against any of\n48\t      * them, and the failure is silent, a lookup that simply finds nothing.\n49\t      */\n50\t    def unescape(s: String): String =\n51\t        if s.indexOf('&') < 0 then s\n52\t        else s.replace(\"&lt;\", \"<\").replace(\"&gt;\", \">\").replace(\"&quot;\", \"\\\"\").replace(\"&apos;\", \"'\").replace(\"&amp;\", \"&\")\n53\t\n54\t    private val AttrName   = \"\"\"name='([^']+)'\"\"\".r\n55\t    private val AttrBytes  = \"\"\"bytes='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n56\t\n57\t    // matched by shape, then classified by attribute. Anchoring on `bci=` saw only 512 of the 633\n58\t    // planted traps: 121 of them lead with `method=` instead and carry `bci` further in. That is the\n59\t    // same defect as the old `<call>` and `<method>` patterns, which is why nothing here anchors on\n60\t    // attribute order any more.\n61\t    private val Trap       = \"\"\"<uncommon_trap [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n62\t    private val AttrThread = \"\"\"thread='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n63\t    private val AttrReason = \"\"\"reason='([^']+)'\"\"\".r\n64\t    private val AttrAction = \"\"\"action='([^']+)'\"\"\".r\n65\t    private val NotEntrant = \"\"\"<make_not_entrant\"\"\".r\n66\t\n67\t    private val Inlined    = \"\"\"<inline_success [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n68\t    private val NotInlined = \"\"\"<inline_fail [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n69\t\n70\t    // matched by shape for the same reason as everything else here: OSR tasks carry\n71\t    // `compile_kind='osr'` between `compile_id` and `method`, so a pattern fixing that order missed\n72\t    // all 5 of them, reporting 0 OSR tasks and 3 fewer C2 tasks than the fork performed.\n73\t    private val TaskOpen  = \"\"\"<task [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n74\t    private val AttrCompileId = \"\"\"compile_id='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n75\t    private val AttrName2 = \"\"\"method='([^']+)'\"\"\".r\n76\t    private val TaskLevel = \"\"\"level='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n77\t    private val TaskStamp = \"\"\"stamp='([\\d.]+)'\"\"\".r\n78\t    private val TaskOsr   = \"\"\"osr_bci=\"\"\".r\n79\t\n80\t    /** One compilation's worth of facts. */\n81\t    case class Task(\n82\t        compileId: Int,\n83\t        method: String,\n84\t        level: Int,\n85\t        osr: Boolean,\n86\t        stamp: Double,\n87\t        /** Guards the compiler planted while compiling this method. Task-scoped because that is what they are: a property of the code the\n88\t          * compiler saw.\n89\t          */\n90\t        plantedTraps: Chunk[String],\n91\t        calls: Chunk[CallMorphism],\n92\t        inlines: Chunk[JitEntry]\n93\t    )\n94\t\n95\t    /** Everything one log yielded, including how much of it was consumed.\n96\t      *\n97\t      * `runtimeDeopts` lives here rather than on `Task` because a deoptimization is not task-scoped: it happens while compiled code runs. In\n98\t      * a captured log all 6 of them precede the first `<task>` element entirely, so modelling them as task children dropped every one while\n99\t      * the parser looked correct.\n100\t      */\n101\t    case class Parsed(\n102\t        tasks: Chunk[Task],\n103\t        runtimeDeopts: Chunk[String],\n104\t        madeNotEntrant: Int,\n105\t        coverage: Chunk[ParseCoverage]\n106\t    )\n107\t\n108\t    def parse(raw: String): Parsed =\n109\t        var klasses = Map.empty[String, String]\n110\t        var methods = Map.empty[String, (String, String, Int)] // id -> (holder klass id, name, bytes)\n111\t        var current = Maybe.empty[(Int, String, Int, Boolean, Double)]\n112\t        // run-scoped: a deoptimization happens while compiled code runs, not while a task compiles\n113\t        var runtime = Chunk.empty[String]\n114\t        var planted = Chunk.empty[String]\n115\t        var calls   = Chunk.empty[CallMorphism]\n116\t        var inlines = Chunk.empty[JitEntry]\n117\t        // `<call>` names the callee; the verdict follows on the next inline element\n118\t        var pending      = Maybe.empty[String]\n119\t        var out          = Chunk.empty[Task]\n120\t        var notEntrant   = 0\n121\t        var trapsParsed  = 0\n122\t        var callsParsed  = 0\n123\t        var methodsKnown = 0\n124\t\n125\t        def flush(): Unit =\n126\t            current.foreach { (id, m, lvl, osr, st) =>\n127\t                out = out.append(Task(id, m, lvl, osr, st, planted, calls, inlines))\n128\t            }\n129\t            planted = Chunk.empty\n130\t            calls = Chunk.empty\n131\t            inlines = Chunk.empty\n132\t            pending = Maybe.empty\n133\t\n134\t        def name(methodId: String): String =\n135\t            methods.get(methodId) match\n136\t                case Some((holder, n, _)) => s\"${klasses.getOrElse(holder, holder)}::$n\"\n137\t                case None                 => s\"method#$methodId\"\n138\t\n139\t        def attr(re: scala.util.matching.Regex, s: String): Maybe[String] =\n140\t            Maybe.fromOption(re.findFirstMatchIn(s).map(m => unescape(m.group(1))))\n141\t\n142\t        // counted by a deliberately loose scan that shares no pattern with the matchers below.\n143\t        // Incrementing `seen` inside the parse loop made coverage self-referential: narrowing a\n144\t        // matcher shrank numerator and denominator together, so reintroducing the historical\n145\t        // 4456-element drop reported 637/637 and 100% coverage with every check green.\n146\t        def occurrences(needle: String): Int =\n147\t            var n = 0\n148\t            var i = raw.indexOf(needle)\n149\t            while i >= 0 do\n150\t                n += 1\n151\t                i = raw.indexOf(needle, i + needle.length)\n152\t            n\n153\t        val callsSeenLoose   = occurrences(\"<call \")\n154\t        val methodsSeenLoose = occurrences(\"<method \")\n155\t        val trapsSeenLoose   = occurrences(\"<uncommon_trap \")\n156\t\n157\t        raw.linesIterator.foreach { line =>\n158\t            TaskOpen.findFirstMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n159\t                flush()\n160\t                // ids are per-task, so the symbol table starts over with every compilation\n161\t                klasses = Map.empty\n162\t                methods = Map.empty\n163\t                // read from the task element itself, never from the line. A `<method>` element\n164\t                // sharing the line carries its own `level='3'`, and scanning the whole line picked\n165\t                // that up instead: both stored production runs recorded 0 C2 tasks for a fork that\n166\t                // actually performed 88 of them.\n167\t                val lvl = TaskLevel.findFirstMatchIn(el).map(_.group(1).toInt).getOrElse(4)\n168\t                val st  = TaskStamp.findFirstMatchIn(el).map(_.group(1).toDouble).getOrElse(0.0)\n169\t                val id  = attr(AttrCompileId, el).map(_.toInt).getOrElse(-1)\n170\t                val mth = attr(AttrName2, el).getOrElse(\"unknown\")\n171\t                current = Maybe((id, mth, lvl, TaskOsr.findFirstMatchIn(el).isDefined, st))\n172\t            }\n173\t\n174\t            Klass.findAllMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n175\t                for\n176\t                    id <- attr(AttrId, el)\n177\t                    nm <- attr(AttrName, el)\n178\t                yield klasses += id -> nm\n179\t            }\n180\t\n181\t            Method.findAllMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n182\t                val parsedMethod =\n183\t                    for\n184\t                        id     <- attr(AttrId, el)\n185\t                        holder <- attr(AttrHolder, el)\n186\t                        n      <- attr(AttrName, el)\n187\t                    yield\n188\t                        // the unloaded form declares no size; Anything else is\n204\t                    // a guard planted during compilation, which is a property of the code, not an event.\n205\t                    if attr(AttrThread, el).isDefined then runtime = runtime.append(k)\n206\t                    else planted = planted.append(k)\n207\t                }\n208\t            }\n209\t            notEntrant += NotEntrant.findAllMatchIn(line).size\n210\t\n211\t            Call.findAllMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n212\t                attr(AttrMethod, el).foreach { id =>\n213\t                    callsParsed += 1\n214\t                    pending = Maybe(id)\n215\t                    // `count='-1'` is HotSpot's no-profile marker; 27 C2 sites carry it. Reading it\n216\t                    // as a count would make a site look profiled-with-negative-calls.\n217\t                    val count = attr(AttrCount, el).map(_.toLong).filter(_ >= 0).getOrElse(0L)\n218\t                    val recvd = attr(AttrRecvN, el).map(_.toLong)\n219\t                    calls = calls.append(\n220\t                        CallMorphism(\n221\t                            callee = name(id),\n222\t                            count = count,\n223\t                            receiverCount = recvd.getOrElse(0L),\n224\t                            // classified only where the JIT actually profiled a receiver. Absence is\n225\t                            // not evidence of polymorphism, and encoding it as `false` is what put\n226\t                            // unprofiled sites under a heading promising measured receiver counts.\n227\t                            monomorphic = if attr(AttrRecv, el).isEmpty then Maybe.empty else Maybe(recvd.exists(_ == count))\n228\t                        )\n229\t                    )\n230\t                }\n231\t            }\n232\t\n233\t            def verdict(reason: String, ok: Boolean): Unit =\n234\t                pending.foreach { id =>\n235\t                    inlines = inlines.append(JitEntry(name(id), methods.get(id).map(_._3).getOrElse(0), ok, reason))\n236\t                }\n237\t                pending = Maybe.empty\n238\t            Inlined.findFirstMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach(el => verdict(attr(AttrReason, el).getOrElse(\"\"), true))\n239\t            NotInlined.findFirstMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach(el => verdict(attr(AttrReason, el).getOrElse(\"\"), false))\n240\t        }\n241\t        flush()\n242\t        Parsed(\n243\t            out,\n244\t            runtime,\n245\t            notEntrant,\n246\t            Chunk(\n247\t                ParseCoverage(\"call sites\", callsSeenLoose, callsParsed),\n248\t                ParseCoverage(\"method declarations\", methodsSeenLoose, methodsKnown),\n249\t                ParseCoverage(\"uncommon traps\", trapsSeenLoose, trapsParsed)\n250\t            )\n251\t        )\n252\t    end parse\n253\t\n254\t    /** Inlining decisions per method, keeping every site, **from C2 compilations only**.\n255\t      *\n256\t      * The tier filter is not a refinement, it is the difference between a signal and noise. In a captured run, of 1969 refusals 1929 come\n257\t      * from C1 tier 3 and 40 from C2, and the split by reason is total:\n258\t      *\n259\t      *   - `callee is too large`: 1166 in C1, **0** in C2\n260\t      *   - `no static binding`: 205 in C1, **0** in C2\n261\t      *   - `callee uses too much stack`: 173 in C1, **0** in C2\n262\t      *\n263\t      * C1 runs for roughly the first two warmup iterations (7.59 us/op, then 5.96, against a measured 5.84-5.90), so those refusals are worth\n264\t      * about 29% of one warmup iteration and nothing at all of the reported score. C1 also has no frequency tier, only a 35-byte gate, which\n265\t      * is why a 37-byte method is refused there and inlined hot by C2. Reporting C1 verdicts as a method's inlining behaviour would point\n266\t      * every optimization at code the measured score never executes.\n267\t      *\n268\t      * Deliberately not folded to one verdict either: 11 of 85 kyo methods carry both, and for two the refusal rests on a single site of six.\n269\t      */\n270\t    def inlining(p: Parsed, prefix: String = \"kyo.\"): Chunk[InlineSites] =\n271\t        Chunk.from(\n272\t            p.tasks.filter(_.level >= 4).flatMap(_.inlines).filter(_.method.startsWith(prefix))\n273\t                .groupBy(_.method).toSeq\n274\t                .map { (method, es) =>\n275\t                    InlineSites(\n276\t                        method = method,\n277\t                        // sites disagree on size when a method is recompiled; the largest is the one that matters for a budget verdict\n278\t                        bytes = es.map(_.bytes).maxOption.getOrElse(0),\n279\t                        inlined = es.count(_.inlined),\n280\t                        refused = es.count(!_.inlined),\n281\t                        reasons = Chunk.from(es.filter(!_.inlined).map(_.reason).distinct)\n282\t                    )\n283\t                }\n284\t                .sortBy(v => (-v.refused, v.method))\n285\t        )\n286\t\n287\t    /** Everything the compilation log says about what compiling this run cost. */\n288\t    def metrics(p: Parsed, profiledMs: Double, totalMs: Double): JitMetrics =\n289\t        val byMethod = p.tasks.groupBy(_.method)\n290\t        JitMetrics(\n291\t            msInWindow = profiledMs,\n292\t            msTotal = totalMs,\n293\t            tasks = p.tasks.size,\n294\t            c2Tasks = p.tasks.count(_.level >= 4),\n295\t            osrTasks = p.tasks.count(_.osr),\n296\t            // recompilation at the SAME tier. Counting every method with more than one task counted\n297\t            // ordinary tier escalation: of 84 such methods in a capture, 74 are a level-3 compile\n298\t            // followed by a level-4 one, which tiered compilation performs on every hot method by\n299\t            // design and which says nothing about an unstable profile.\n300\t            recompiled = byMethod.count((_, ts) => ts.groupBy(_.level).exists(_._2.size > 1)),\n301\t            runtimeDeopts = p.runtimeDeopts.size,\n302\t            plantedTraps = p.tasks.map(_.plantedTraps.size).sum,\n303\t            madeNotEntrant = p.madeNotEntrant,\n304\t            lastCompileAt = if p.tasks.isEmpty then 0.0 else p.tasks.map(_.stamp).max\n305\t        )\n306\t    end metrics\n307\t\n308\t    /** Runtime deoptimization reasons and how often each fired, worst first.\n309\t      *\n310\t      * Runtime events only. Compiler-planted guards are a property of the code the compiler saw, not of the run, and comparing their counts\n311\t      * between legs compares guard censuses while calling the difference a deoptimization change.\n312\t      */\n313\t    def deoptSummary(p: Parsed): Chunk[Deopt] =\n314\t        Chunk.from(\n315\t            p.runtimeDeopts.groupBy(identity).toSeq\n316\t                .map((reason, hits) => Deopt(reason, hits.size))\n317\t                .sortBy(-_.count)\n318\t        )\n319\t\n320\t    /** Call sites the JIT profiled a receiver for, aggregated by callee, worst-polymorphism first.\n321\t      *\n322\t      * Only profiled sites appear. In a captured run that is 12 of 5093 call elements, so this answers a narrow question about a handful of\n323\t      * sites and cannot speak for the rest. Reporting the unprofiled majority as polymorphic is the failure this exists to prevent.\n324\t      */\n325\t    def morphism(p: Parsed, prefix: String = \"kyo.\"): Chunk[CallMorphism] =\n326\t        Chunk.from(\n327\t            p.tasks.flatMap(_.calls).filter(c => c.profiled && c.callee.startsWith(prefix))\n328\t                .groupBy(_.callee).toSeq\n329\t                .map { (callee, cs) =>\n330\t                    CallMorphism(callee, cs.map(_.count).sum, cs.map(_.receiverCount).sum, Maybe(cs.forall(_.monomorphic.contains(true))))\n331\t                }\n332\t                .sortBy(c => (c.monomorphic.contains(true), -c.count))\n333\t        )\n334\t\n335\t    /** Methods whose C2 inlining verdict differs between two logs.\n336\t      *\n337\t      * The efficacy gate. When an isolation run changes a JVM flag, this answers the only question that licenses reading its score: did the\n338\t      * flag do anything? A harness whose flags silently fail to take would refute every hypothesis it tested and pass its own acceptance,\n339\t      * which is the most dangerous failure available to it.\n340\t      *\n341\t      * It also names *what* moved, which is how a budget experiment turns into a mechanism: raising `FreqInlineSize` from 325 to 600 moved 57\n342\t      * methods, and the one that mattered was a 379-byte continuation body going from refused-at-every-site to inlined.\n343\t      */\n344\t    def diffVerdicts(before: Parsed, after: Parsed, prefix: String = \"kyo.\"): Chunk[VerdictChange] =\n345\t        val b = inlining(before, prefix).map(v => v.method -> v).toMap\n346\t        val a = inlining(after, prefix).map(v => v.method -> v).toMap\n347\t        Chunk.from(\n348\t            (b.keySet ++ a.keySet).toSeq.sorted.flatMap { m =>\n349\t                val bs = b.getOrElse(m, InlineSites(m, 0, 0, 0, Chunk.empty))\n350\t                val as = a.getOrElse(m, InlineSites(m, 0, 0, 0, Chunk.empty))\n351\t                if bs.inlined == as.inlined && bs.refused == as.refused then None\n352\t                else Some(VerdictChange(m, Math.max(bs.bytes, as.bytes), bs, as))\n353\t            }\n354\t        )\n355\t\n356\t    /** Whether a configuration change had any effect on inlining at all.\n357\t      *\n358\t      * Reported as a count and a size-refusal delta rather than a boolean, because \"the flag took\" is a matter of degree: one verdict moving\n359\t      * is noise, fifty-seven moving with size refusals falling from 31 to 20 is a flag doing its job.\n360\t      */\n361\t    def efficacy(before: Parsed, after: Parsed, prefix: String = \"kyo.\"): (Int, Int, Int) =\n362\t        val changed = diffVerdicts(before, after, prefix).size\n363\t        // counted per site, not per method: a method that went from ten refusals to six still has\n364\t        // some, so a method-level count reports no change where more than a third of the refusals\n365\t        // actually went away\n366\t        def sizeRefusals(p: Parsed) =\n367\t            inlining(p, prefix).filter(_.reasons.exists(r => r.contains(\"too big\") || r.contains(\"too large\"))).map(_.refused).sum\n368\t        (changed, sizeRefusals(before), sizeRefusals(after))\n369\t\n370\t    /** Methods refused for size while close enough to a budget that shrinking them could flip the verdict, worst first. */\n371\t    def budgetCandidates(p: Parsed, prefix: String = \"kyo.\"): Chunk[InlineSites] =\n372\t        Chunk.from(inlining(p, prefix).filter(_.nearBudget.isDefined).sortBy(-_.refused))\n373\t\n374\t    /** Sites the log carries no receiver profile for. Reported as a count, never as a classification. */\n375\t    def unprofiledSites(p: Parsed, prefix: String = \"kyo.\"): Int =\n376\t        p.tasks.flatMap(_.calls).count(c => !c.profiled && c.callee.startsWith(prefix))\n377\t\n378\tend LogCompilation\n379\t"}]},"uuid":"32354bb9-9139-4830-9ff3-29509af45717","timestamp":"2026-08-17T16:05:48.502Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/effervescent-painting-backus/kyo-kernel2/.claude/skills/kernel/bench-harness/LogCompilation.scala","content":"import Model.*\nimport kyo.*\n\n/** Parses HotSpot's `-XX:+LogCompilation` XML.\n  *\n  * This is the sole source of inlining decisions. `PrintInlining` reports a verdict and a byte count and nothing reliable beyond that: its\n  * output interleaves across compiler threads, so its tree cannot be trusted. Here every decision sits beside the `<method>` element that\n  * declares the callee's size, in structure, and the log additionally carries what that one cannot:\n  *\n  *   - deoptimizations that actually happened, which are invisible everywhere else\n  *   - receiver counts per call site, so monomorphic against megamorphic is measured rather than asserted\n  *   - OSR compilations, which is where a benchmark's loop body actually lives\n  *\n  * Ids are scoped to a compilation task and reused across tasks, so the symbol table is rebuilt per `<task>`.\n  *\n  * Three distinctions here were each responsible for a wrong conclusion, and are preserved deliberately:\n  *\n  *   1. A call site with no `receiver` attribute is *unprofiled*, not megamorphic.\n  *   2. An `<uncommon_trap>` with `thread=` is an event; one with `bci=` is a guard the compiler planted.\n  *   3. A method's inlining verdict is per site. It has a denominator, and reporting it without one is a coin flip.\n  */\nobject LogCompilation:\n\n    // `<call>` appears in two forms: the C2 form carrying `count` (and sometimes `receiver`), and the C1 form carrying only `instr`.\n    // Matching just the first silently dropped 4456 of 5093 elements, so the shape is matched first and the attributes read after.\n    private val Call       = \"\"\"<call [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrMethod = \"\"\"method='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n    // boundary-anchored: an unanchored `count='` also matches `receiver_count='`, which reads\n    // correctly today only because count always precedes it. On a site where it did not, the parser\n    // would take the receiver count as the call count and then call the site monomorphic, since\n    // `recvd == count` becomes trivially true.\n    private val AttrCount  = \"\"\"(?<![\\w_])count='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrRecv   = \"\"\"receiver='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrRecvN  = \"\"\"receiver_count='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n\n    // by shape, for the same reason as the rest: fixing `id` before `name` is one reordering away\n    // from silently dropping the symbol table\n    private val Klass = \"\"\"<klass [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n    // `bytes` and `iicount` are absent on the `unloaded='1'` form, so requiring both dropped 89 of 4466 declarations and left 118 call\n    // sites resolving to raw ids downstream.\n    private val Method     = \"\"\"<method [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrId     = \"\"\"(?<![\\w_])id='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrHolder = \"\"\"holder='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n    /** The log is XML, so its attribute values are escaped, and a constructor arrives as `&lt;init&gt;`.\n      *\n      * Every other tool in this ladder prints `<init>`: javap, async-profiler, the JVM's own\n      * `PrintInlining`. A name that agrees with none of them cannot be cross-referenced against any of\n      * them, and the failure is silent, a lookup that simply finds nothing.\n      */\n    def unescape(s: String): String =\n        if s.indexOf('&') < 0 then s\n        else s.replace(\"&lt;\", \"<\").replace(\"&gt;\", \">\").replace(\"&quot;\", \"\\\"\").replace(\"&apos;\", \"'\").replace(\"&amp;\", \"&\")\n\n    private val AttrName   = \"\"\"name='([^']+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrBytes  = \"\"\"bytes='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n\n    // matched by shape, then classified by attribute. Anchoring on `bci=` saw only 512 of the 633\n    // planted traps: 121 of them lead with `method=` instead and carry `bci` further in. That is the\n    // same defect as the old `<call>` and `<method>` patterns, which is why nothing here anchors on\n    // attribute order any more.\n    private val Trap       = \"\"\"<uncommon_trap [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrThread = \"\"\"thread='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrReason = \"\"\"reason='([^']+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrAction = \"\"\"action='([^']+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val NotEntrant = \"\"\"<make_not_entrant\"\"\".r\n\n    private val Inlined    = \"\"\"<inline_success [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n    private val NotInlined = \"\"\"<inline_fail [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n\n    // matched by shape for the same reason as everything else here: OSR tasks carry\n    // `compile_kind='osr'` between `compile_id` and `method`, so a pattern fixing that order missed\n    // all 5 of them, reporting 0 OSR tasks and 3 fewer C2 tasks than the fork performed.\n    private val TaskOpen  = \"\"\"<task [^>]*>\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrCompileId = \"\"\"compile_id='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val AttrName2 = \"\"\"method='([^']+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val TaskLevel = \"\"\"level='(\\d+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val TaskStamp = \"\"\"stamp='([\\d.]+)'\"\"\".r\n    private val TaskOsr   = \"\"\"osr_bci=\"\"\".r\n\n    /** One compilation's worth of facts. */\n    case class Task(\n        compileId: Int,\n        method: String,\n        level: Int,\n        osr: Boolean,\n        stamp: Double,\n        /** Guards the compiler planted while compiling this method. Task-scoped because that is what they are: a property of the code the\n          * compiler saw.\n          */\n        plantedTraps: Chunk[String],\n        calls: Chunk[CallMorphism],\n        inlines: Chunk[JitEntry]\n    )\n\n    /** Everything one log yielded, including how much of it was consumed.\n      *\n      * `runtimeDeopts` lives here rather than on `Task` because a deoptimization is not task-scoped: it happens while compiled code runs. In\n      * a captured log all 6 of them precede the first `<task>` element entirely, so modelling them as task children dropped every one while\n      * the parser looked correct.\n      */\n    case class Parsed(\n        tasks: Chunk[Task],\n        runtimeDeopts: Chunk[String],\n        madeNotEntrant: Int,\n        coverage: Chunk[ParseCoverage]\n    )\n\n    def parse(raw: String): Parsed =\n        var klasses = Map.empty[String, String]\n        var methods = Map.empty[String, (String, String, Int)] // id -> (holder klass id, name, bytes)\n        var current = Maybe.empty[(Int, String, Int, Boolean, Double)]\n        // run-scoped: a deoptimization happens while compiled code runs, not while a task compiles\n        var runtime = Chunk.empty[String]\n        var planted = Chunk.empty[String]\n        var calls   = Chunk.empty[CallMorphism]\n        var inlines = Chunk.empty[JitEntry]\n        // `<call>` names the callee; the verdict follows on the next inline element\n        var pending      = Maybe.empty[String]\n        var out          = Chunk.empty[Task]\n        var notEntrant   = 0\n        var trapsParsed  = 0\n        var callsParsed  = 0\n        var methodsKnown = 0\n\n        def flush(): Unit =\n            current.foreach { (id, m, lvl, osr, st) =>\n                out = out.append(Task(id, m, lvl, osr, st, planted, calls, inlines))\n            }\n            planted = Chunk.empty\n            calls = Chunk.empty\n            inlines = Chunk.empty\n            pending = Maybe.empty\n\n        def name(methodId: String): String =\n            methods.get(methodId) match\n                case Some((holder, n, _)) => s\"${klasses.getOrElse(holder, holder)}::$n\"\n                case None                 => s\"method#$methodId\"\n\n        def attr(re: scala.util.matching.Regex, s: String): Maybe[String] =\n            Maybe.fromOption(re.findFirstMatchIn(s).map(m => unescape(m.group(1))))\n\n        // counted by a deliberately loose scan that shares no pattern with the matchers below.\n        // Incrementing `seen` inside the parse loop made coverage self-referential: narrowing a\n        // matcher shrank numerator and denominator together, so reintroducing the historical\n        // 4456-element drop reported 637/637 and 100% coverage with every check green.\n        def occurrences(needle: String): Int =\n            var n = 0\n            var i = raw.indexOf(needle)\n            while i >= 0 do\n                n += 1\n                i = raw.indexOf(needle, i + needle.length)\n            n\n        val callsSeenLoose   = occurrences(\"<call \")\n        val methodsSeenLoose = occurrences(\"<method \")\n        val trapsSeenLoose   = occurrences(\"<uncommon_trap \")\n\n        raw.linesIterator.foreach { line =>\n            TaskOpen.findFirstMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n                flush()\n                // ids are per-task, so the symbol table starts over with every compilation\n                klasses = Map.empty\n                methods = Map.empty\n                // read from the task element itself, never from the line. A `<method>` element\n                // sharing the line carries its own `level='3'`, and scanning the whole line picked\n                // that up instead: both stored production runs recorded 0 C2 tasks for a fork that\n                // actually performed 88 of them.\n                val lvl = TaskLevel.findFirstMatchIn(el).map(_.group(1).toInt).getOrElse(4)\n                val st  = TaskStamp.findFirstMatchIn(el).map(_.group(1).toDouble).getOrElse(0.0)\n                val id  = attr(AttrCompileId, el).map(_.toInt).getOrElse(-1)\n                val mth = attr(AttrName2, el).getOrElse(\"unknown\")\n                current = Maybe((id, mth, lvl, TaskOsr.findFirstMatchIn(el).isDefined, st))\n            }\n\n            Klass.findAllMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n                for\n                    id <- attr(AttrId, el)\n                    nm <- attr(AttrName, el)\n                yield klasses += id -> nm\n            }\n\n            Method.findAllMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n                val parsedMethod =\n                    for\n                        id     <- attr(AttrId, el)\n                        holder <- attr(AttrHolder, el)\n                        n      <- attr(AttrName, el)\n                    yield\n                        // the unloaded form declares no size; 0 is the honest reading, and keeping\n                        // the entry is what stops the id going unresolved later\n                        methods += id -> (holder, n, attr(AttrBytes, el).map(_.toInt).getOrElse(0))\n                        ()\n                if parsedMethod.isDefined then methodsKnown += 1\n            }\n\n            Trap.findAllMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n                val kind =\n                    for\n                        reason <- attr(AttrReason, el)\n                        action <- attr(AttrAction, el)\n                    yield s\"$reason/$action\"\n                kind.foreach { k =>\n                    trapsParsed += 1\n                    // `thread=` means a running method fell back to the interpreter. Anything else is\n                    // a guard planted during compilation, which is a property of the code, not an event.\n                    if attr(AttrThread, el).isDefined then runtime = runtime.append(k)\n                    else planted = planted.append(k)\n                }\n            }\n            notEntrant += NotEntrant.findAllMatchIn(line).size\n\n            Call.findAllMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach { el =>\n                attr(AttrMethod, el).foreach { id =>\n                    callsParsed += 1\n                    pending = Maybe(id)\n                    // `count='-1'` is HotSpot's no-profile marker; 27 C2 sites carry it. Reading it\n                    // as a count would make a site look profiled-with-negative-calls.\n                    val count = attr(AttrCount, el).map(_.toLong).filter(_ >= 0).getOrElse(0L)\n                    val recvd = attr(AttrRecvN, el).map(_.toLong)\n                    calls = calls.append(\n                        CallMorphism(\n                            callee = name(id),\n                            count = count,\n                            receiverCount = recvd.getOrElse(0L),\n                            // classified only where the JIT actually profiled a receiver. Absence is\n                            // not evidence of polymorphism, and encoding it as `false` is what put\n                            // unprofiled sites under a heading promising measured receiver counts.\n                            monomorphic = if attr(AttrRecv, el).isEmpty then Maybe.empty else Maybe(recvd.exists(_ == count))\n                        )\n                    )\n                }\n            }\n\n            def verdict(reason: String, ok: Boolean): Unit =\n                pending.foreach { id =>\n                    inlines = inlines.append(JitEntry(name(id), methods.get(id).map(_._3).getOrElse(0), ok, reason))\n                }\n                pending = Maybe.empty\n            Inlined.findFirstMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach(el => verdict(attr(AttrReason, el).getOrElse(\"\"), true))\n            NotInlined.findFirstMatchIn(line).map(_.matched).foreach(el => verdict(attr(AttrReason, el).getOrElse(\"\"), false))\n        }\n        flush()\n        Parsed(\n            out,\n            runtime,\n            notEntrant,\n            Chunk(\n                ParseCoverage(\"call sites\", callsSeenLoose, callsParsed),\n                ParseCoverage(\"method declarations\", methodsSeenLoose, methodsKnown),\n                ParseCoverage(\"uncommon traps\", trapsSeenLoose, trapsParsed)\n            )\n        )\n    end parse\n\n    /** Inlining decisions per method, keeping every site, **from C2 compilations only**.\n      *\n      * The tier filter is not a refinement, it is the difference between a signal and noise. removed: Chunk[String]) derives Schema:\n        def sizeDelta: Int = variantSize - controlSize\n\n        /** Whether the change crossed a HotSpot inlining budget, which is the only reason a size change matters on its own. */\n        def crossedBudget: Maybe[String] =\n            val budgets = Seq(35 -> \"MaxInlineSize\", 325 -> \"FreqInlineSize\")\n            Maybe.fromOption(\n                budgets.collectFirst {\n                    case (limit, nm) if controlSize <= limit && variantSize > limit  => s\"grew past $nm ($limit)\"\n                    case (limit, nm) if controlSize > limit && variantSize <= limit  => s\"dropped below $nm ($limit)\"\n                }\n            )\n\n        def show: String =\n            val budget = crossedBudget.map(b => s\", $b\").getOrElse(\"\")\n            val plus   = if added.isEmpty then \"\" else s\" +${added.mkString(\",\")}\"\n            val minus  = if removed.isEmpty then \"\" else s\" -${removed.mkString(\",\")}\"\n            f\"$method%s ${controlSize}B -> ${variantSize}B ($sizeDelta%+d)$budget$plus$minus\"\n    end Change\n\n    /** Methods whose compiled form differs, by name. Methods identical in both are omitted rather than listed as unchanged. */\n    def diff(control: Chunk[Method], variant: Chunk[Method]): Chunk[Change] =\n        val byName = control.map(m => (m.name + m.signature) -> m).toMap\n        Chunk.from(\n            variant.flatMap { v =>\n                byName.get(v.name + v.signature).flatMap { c =>\n                    val cm = c.mnemonics\n                    val vm = v.mnemonics\n                    if cm == vm && c.size == v.size then None\n                    else\n                        // multiset difference: an instruction appearing three times in one and twice\n                        // in the other is one removal, not zero\n                        Some(Change(\n                            method = v.name + v.signature,\n                            controlSize = c.size,\n                            variantSize = v.size,\n                            added = Chunk.from(vm.diff(cm).distinct),\n                            removed = Chunk.from(cm.diff(vm).distinct)\n                        ))\n                }\n            }\n        )\n    end diff\n\n    /** Cross-checks computed sizes against HotSpot's own `bytes` attribute from the compilation log.\n      *\n      * Two independent derivations of the same number. An ingested run genuinely does not know those things, and\n  * the report must not imply otherwise.\n  */\nobject Ingest:\n\n    case class Failed(what: String) extends Exception(what) with scala.util.control.NoStackTrace\n\n    /** Build a `Run` from a JMH json document.\n      *\n      * `declaredRows` is what the benchmark class declares. A json holding fewer rows than that is a\n      * subset run, and the report already refuses to make a suite-wide claim from one; getting this\n      * wrong in the permissive direction is how a four-row subset once passed as a clean suite.\n      */\n    def run(\n        raw: String,\n        label: String,\n        sha: String,\n        session: Session,\n        source: String,\n        declaredRows: Int\n    )(using Frame): Run < Bench.Fail =\n        Bench.parseJmh(raw).map { rows =>\n            if rows.isEmpty then Abort.fail(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"$source holds no benchmark rows\"))\n            else\n                Run(\n                    id = s\"$label-${sha.take(10)}-${source.hashCode.toHexString}\",\n                    session = session,\n                    label = label,\n                    sha = sha,\n                    // not a tree hash: this run was not produced from a tree this harness controlled,\n                    // and pretending otherwise would let it claim a guard it never passed\n                    treeHash = s\"ingested:$source\",\n                    forks = 1,\n                    evidence = Evidence.Timing,\n                    wholeClass = rows.size >= declaredRows,\n                    declaredRows = declaredRows,\n                    markers = Chunk.empty,\n                    warmup = Bench.WarmupIterations,\n                    jit_metrics = Maybe.empty,\n                    rows = rows,\n                    jit = Chunk.empty,\n                    coverage = Chunk.empty,\n                    alloc = Chunk.empty, allocByMethod = Chunk.empty,\n                    cpu = Chunk.empty,\n                    deopts = Chunk.empty,\n                    morphism = Chunk.empty,\n                    recordedAt = source\n Isolated on purpose: scala-cli with published kyo artifacts, no dependency on the\n5\trepo's sbt build, which does not compile as a whole while the kernel migration is in flight.\n6\t\n7\t```sh\n8\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchTest                       # guards self-check, no benchmark needed\n9\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchRun -- --worktree ../../../../../bench-sweep \\\n10\t    --label control --sha 36b41336fb                         # measure one leg, store it\n11\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchCompare -- --control <id> --variant <id>\n12\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchBracket -- --worktree ../../../../../bench-sweep \\\n13\t    --control <sha> --variant <sha>                          # C V C V C, with a real threshold\n14\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchChain -- --worktree ../../../../../bench-sweep \\\n15\t    --sha <a> --sha <b> --sha <c>                            # isolate one change per step\n16\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchPlan -- --from <id> --target 5\n17\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchIngest -- --json <f> --label <l> --sha <sha>\n18\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchList\n19\tscala-cli run . --main-class BenchShow -- --id <id>\n20\t```\n21\t\n22\t## Why it collects more than timing\n23\t\n24\tWall clock says whether something moved, never why. Every mechanism established in this\n25\tproject came from `gc.alloc.rate.norm`, allocation sites, the CPU profile, or the inlining\n26\tlog, and every mechanism claimed *without* them turned out wrong on the next measurement. So\n27\t`run` walks the whole ladder by default: the measurement carries the gc profiler, then an\n28\tallocation-site profile, a CPU profile, and a short `PrintInlining` pass. `--evidence timing`\n29\tskips them for iteration, and any report built from such a run is stamped as unattributed.\n30\t\n31\t## What it refuses to do\n32\t\n33\tEach guard exists because its absence corrupted or wasted a real measurement:\n34\t\n35\t- **Run in a worktree that is on a branch.** A bracket worktree is created detached, so a\n36\t  detached HEAD is the property required. Comparing git dirs was tried first and catches only\n37\t  the repository's *primary* worktree, while the tree that must not be scribbled on is whichever\n38\t  one work happens in, and that one is always on a branch. Brackets overwrite sources; doing\n39\t  that where commits come from destroyed uncommitted work and, once, a whole redesign.\n40\t- **Flip designs with `git checkout <sha> -- <paths>`.** Checkout stages what it restores, so\n41\t  an interrupted bracket leaves the comparison design in the index and the next commit sweeps\n42\t  it in. Only `git restore --worktree` is used.\n43\t- **Measure a red tree.** The suite must pass before a leg spends any runs, because a faster\n44\t  variant with failing tests is not a result.\n45\t- **Trust a short read.** Row count is checked against bare `@Benchmark` lines in the class,\n46\t  retried, then failed. Matching the substring would also match `@BenchmarkMode`.\n47\t- **Report a suite-wide verdict from a subset run.** \"No row regressed\" is unreachable unless\n48\t  both legs measured the whole class; a subset says so in its own conclusion instead.\n49\t- **Let an artifact headline.** Scores dominated by their own error render as below resolution\n50\t  and sort past the real movements, so a 5ns row reading +20% cannot pose as the worst\n51\t  regression.\n52\t- **Narrate a movement with no evidence behind it.** A row that moved while allocation and\n53\t  inlining did not is marked unexplained, which is the tool's way of enforcing the rule that a\n54\t  mechanism must be measured rather than reasoned.\n55\t- **Attribute a two-sha difference to one change inside it.** A pair does not declare a\n56\t  partition, so the report says no source-level mechanism follows from it, however plausible one\n57\t  is. `chain` declares the partition and each of its steps is attributable.\n58\t- **Read a session that cannot check itself.** A dirty A/A null, or too few control legs to run\n59\t  one, is a blocker with an exit code rather than a line of text: every row an A/A classifies is\n60\t  a false positive by construction, so it is the strongest available statement that nothing\n61\t  below is readable.\n62\t- **Return a verdict from a falsifier whose flag never took.** `CompileCommand=inline` is a\n63\t  hint, and HotSpot still refuses on `MaxInlineLevel`, node budget, or a method it cannot\n64\t  compile. Such a run is inconclusive, never a refutation.\n65\t- **Store a measurement without the configuration that produced it.** A configuration\n66\t  comparison varies nothing but JVM arguments, so a stored pair with the same sha and tree hash\n67\t  is otherwise indistinguishable. The campaign's headline result was stored exactly that way and\n68\t  is unrecoverable because of it. Runs record their arguments, and a same-sha comparison prints\n69\t  which ones differ.\n70\t- **Round a verdict's own numbers away.** A cleanly separated 26.2% regression on a nanosecond\n71\t  row once rendered as `0.01 ± 0.00` against `0.01 ± 0.00`. Precision scales with magnitude, so\n72\t  the figures behind a verdict stay legible and the error column never reads as zero when it is\n73\t  not.\n74\t\n75\t## What it proposes next\n76\t\n77\tA comparison that stops at \"this row moved\" is where \"it is slower, so replace it\" comes from.\n78\tEvery delta arrives with the experiments that could contradict the obvious reading of it, each\n79\tone JVM flag and one run: force the method the variant stopped inlining, raise only the budget\n80\tit is over, force the *control*'s refused method to test whether a win was the inlining rather\n81\tthan the design, disable escape analysis when allocation moved.\n82\t\n83\t## Storage\n84\t\n85\tEvery leg is stored with its markers, configuration and full ladder, so `compare` is a pure\n86\tfunction over records and never re-runs anything. Two run ids always produce the same verdict,\n87\tand what the JIT decided about a method stays answerable long after the run.\n88\t"}]},"uuid":"b12252cf-76df-4da3-a091-4bf111134d49","timestamp":"2026-08-17T16:05:57.615Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/effervescent-painting-backus/kyo-kernel2/.claude/skills/kernel/bench-harness/README.md","content":"# bench-harness\n\nThe measurement protocol from the kernel skill, as a program rather than as bash typed fresh\neach time. \"sweep-replicated\"\n\n    var failures = 0\n\n    def check(name: String, cond: Boolean, detail: String = \"\"): Unit =\n        if cond then println(s\"  ok   $name\")\n        else\n            failures += 1\n            println(s\"  FAIL $name${if detail.nonEmpty then s\"\\n         $detail\" else \"\"}\")\n\n    run {\n        for\n            runs <- Store.list(store)\n            controls = runs.filter(_.label.startsWith(\"control\")).sortBy(_.label)\n            variants = runs.filter(_.label.startsWith(\"variant\")).sortBy(_.label)\n\n            _ = println(\"the fixture: a real five-leg bracket\")\n            _ = check(\"three control legs\", controls.size == 3, s\"${controls.size}\")\n            _ = check(\"two variant legs\", variants.size == 2, s\"${variants.size}\")\n            _ = check(\n                \"and it recorded the configuration that produced it\",\n                variants.forall(_.jvmArgs.exists(_.contains(\"CompileCommandFile\"))) && controls.forall(_.jvmArgs.isEmpty),\n                s\"control ${controls.map(_.jvmArgs).mkString}, variant ${variants.map(_.jvmArgs).mkString}\"\n            )\n\n            cmp      = Bench.compareReplicated(controls, variants)\n            forecast = Plan.forecast(runs, legs = 5, Bench.FamilyAlpha)\n            byRow    = forecast.map(f => f.row -> f).toMap\n\n            _ = println(\"\\nthe forecast reproduces the threshold the bracket computed\")\n            // every row the comparison resolved must have a forecast, and the two must agree closely.\n            // The tolerance is a tenth of the threshold: these are two derivations of one quantity,\n            // not two measurements of it, so they should differ only by rounding and by the fact that\n            // the forecast normalises against every leg while the threshold normalises against the\n            // control mean.\n            compared = cmp.deltas.flatMap(d => Chunk.from(d.resolution.map(r => (d.row, r.percent))))\n            _        = check(\"every row carries a resolution to compare against\", compared.size == cmp.deltas.size, s\"${compared.size} of ${cmp.deltas.size}\")\n            _ = compared.foreach { (row, actual) =>\n                byRow.get(row) match\n                    case None => check(s\"$row has a forecast\", false)\n                    case Some(f) =>\n                        val predicted = f.resolvable * 100\n                        val slack     = Math.max(0.5, actual * 0.10)\n                        check(\n                            f\"$row%-34s forecast ±${predicted}%.1f%% against actual ±${actual}%.1f%%\",\n                            Math.abs(predicted - actual) <= slack,\n                            f\"off by ${Math.abs(predicted - actual)}%.2f points, tolerance ${slack}%.2f\"\n                        )\n            }\n\n            _ = println(\"\\nthe estimator says which basis it used\")\n            // a one-arm forecast cannot see the other arm's variance and is optimistic because of it.\n            // Saying so is the difference between a number and a number you can act on.\n            oneArm = Plan.forecast(controls, legs = 5, Bench.FamilyAlpha)\n            _      = check(\"both arms pool\", forecast.forall(f => f.fromReplicates && !f.oneArm), forecast.take(1).map(_.show).mkString)\n            _      = check(\"one arm admits it is one arm\", oneArm.forall(_.oneArm), oneArm.take(1).map(_.show).mkString)\n            _      = check(\"and says so in its own output\", oneArm.headOption.exists(_.show.contains(\"optimistic\")), oneArm.take(1).map(_.show).mkString)\n\n            // The must-fire twin, and it corrects a claim I made before measuring it. I wrote that a\n            // control-only forecast is \"systematically optimistic\". On this bracket it under-predicts\n            // on 4 rows of 15 and over-predicts on others, so the honest property is not a direction\n            // but a difference: seeing one arm's spread instead of two is a materially different\n            // estimate, which is why the label exists. If one-arm and two-arm ever agreed everywhere,\n            // the label would be decoration.\n            differing = compared.count { (row, _) =>\n                (oneArm.find(_.row == row), byRow.get(row)) match\n                    case (Some(one), Some(both)) => Math.abs(one.resolvable - both.resolvable) * 100 > 0.5\n                    case _                       => false\n            }\n            underPredicting = compared.count { (row, actual) =>\n                oneArm.find(_.row == row).exists(_.resolvable * 100 < actual - 0.5)\n            }\n            _ = println(f\"       one arm differs from two on $differing%d of ${compared.size}%d rows, under-predicting on $underPredicting%d\")\n            _ = check(\n                \"a one-arm forecast is a materially different estimate, not a relabelled one\",\n                differing >= 3,\n                s\"$differing of ${compared.size} rows differ by more than 0.5 points\"\n            )\n            _ = check(\n                \"and it errs in both directions, so the bias is not a direction to correct for\",\n                underPredicting > 0 && underPredicting < compared.size,\n                s\"under-predicts on $underPredicting of ${compared.size}\"\n            )\n\n            _ = println(if failures == 0 then \"\\nall checks passed\" else s\"\\n$failures FAILED\")\n            _ <- Abort.when(failures > 0)(Bench.BracketFailed(s\"$failures checks failed\"))\n        yield ()\n    }\nend PlanTest\n","numLines":114,"startLine":1,"totalLines":114}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1d7fd2db-dfc0-4ede-9e13-9d19256eff3c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/fwbrasil/workspace/kyo/.claude/worktrees/majestic-zooming-quiche","sessionId":"32789380-338f-4ca0-80c5-d4b8d798354f","version":"2.1.231","gitBranch":"ci/fork-guards","slug":"majestic-zooming-quiche"}
